Quantitative viral titration of tissues at three days post-infection established that viral replication peaked in the upper respiratory tract and associated ocular tissues, reaching 10^5.56 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in the nasal turbinates and 10^4.23 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in the Harderian gland, while trachea and bronchus titers both reached 10^1.82 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter, confirming strict respiratory tropism. The marked discrepancy between mild experimental laboratory infections in specific-pathogen-free chickens and the severe mortality observed in the commercial Henan flock highlights the profound influence of secondary production factors. In industrial poultry operations, high-density stocking, environmental ammonia accumulation, ventilation stress, and concurrent microbial exposures create an environment highly permissive to exacerbated clinical disease. Primary viral replication by low-pathogenic strains such as NL04 damages the respiratory ciliated epithelium and compromises mucociliary clearance, rendering birds highly vulnerable to secondary opportunistic bacterial invaders such as Escherichia coli and Mycoplasma species. These secondary pathogens frequently induce severe exudative fibrinous airsacculitis and bronchial occlusion, explaining the fatal plugs observed in the commercial outbreak. The experimental findings emphasize that specific-pathogen-free animal trials alone cannot predict the true veterinary and economic impact of emerging avian influenza variants in real-world commercial poultry operations. To evaluate potential mammalian spillover risk, the research team intranasally challenged six-week-old female BALB/c mice with 10^6.00 EID50 of the purified NL04 virus. Over the fourteen-day evaluation period, all infected mice survived without displaying detectable respiratory distress, ruffled fur, or statistically significant weight loss relative to sham-inoculated controls. Organ titration at three days post-infection demonstrated limited replication, with viral titers confined predominantly to the upper respiratory tract at 10^3.25 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in nasal turbinates, accompanied by minimal levels of 10^1.56 in lung tissue and 10^1.18 in kidney tissue. Brain samples showed no viral replication, and histological sections revealed only mild alveolar inflammatory infiltration without structural necrosis. In vitro replication kinetics comparing Madin-Darby canine kidney cells and primary chick embryo fibroblasts revealed rapid viral propagation in both cell types, though avian fibroblasts supported significantly higher viral yields during early replication phases between 12 and 48 hours post-infection. These mammalian studies demonstrate that despite bearing several molecular adaptation markers, NL04 possesses limited mammalian replication competence and low intrinsic pathogenicity in mice. Global epidemiological analysis of 5,029 historical H6Ny avian influenza isolates cataloged from 1963 to 2025 provided broader context on subtype evolution, ecological reservoirs, and interspecies transmission events. Annual isolation numbers remained low through the late 1990s before expanding sharply into an ongoing elevated circulation plateau that peaked in 2014 with approximately 440 recorded isolates. Avian species constituted the predominant ecological niche, representing 91.7 percent of the total dataset, whereas environmental samples accounted for 6.4 percent, and mammalian and human isolations remained exceptionally scarce at four and two cases respectively. Among the nine recognized neuraminidase pairings, H6N2 and H6N6 emerged as the dominant subtypes globally, accounting for 30.98 percent and 28.08 percent of all isolates, followed by H6N1 at 17.24 percent. While wild aquatic waterfowl constitute the natural ancestral reservoir, the surveillance dataset documented 145 separate spillover events of H6N2 into domestic chickens, demonstrating that terrestrial poultry now represent an established secondary niche that facilitates frequent encounters and reassortment with endemic poultry viruses. Given the commercial risks posed by circulating reassortants, the researchers formulated and tested a whole-inactivated oil-emulsion vaccine candidate derived from the homologous NL04 strain. Purified allantoic virus was inactivated using 0.1 percent beta-propiolactone for 24 hours at four degrees Celsius, followed by beta-propiolactone hydrolysis at thirty-seven degrees Celsius and high-speed emulsification with Montanide ISA 78 VG adjuvant. Three-week-old specific-pathogen-free chickens received a single intramuscular injection of 0.3 milliliters of the prepared vaccine formulation, with control animals receiving adjuvant-emulsified saline. Serum hemagglutination inhibition titers monitored weekly reached a mean of 13.25 log2 by five weeks post-immunization, confirming the induction of a potent humoral immune response. Following homologous live virus challenge at five weeks, vaccinated birds exhibited a substantially shortened and restricted shedding profile, shedding virus exclusively through the oral route and clearing infection within four days, whereas unvaccinated control birds shed virus predominantly through the oral route across the first week post-challenge. Neutralization assays conducted in embryonated chicken eggs further demonstrated that post-vaccination antisera effectively neutralized the homologous NL04 virus and exhibited cross-protective neutralizing activity against a heterologous H6N1 isolate collected from poultry in December 2025. In both cases, incubation of serum-virus mixtures abolished detectable hemagglutinating activity in harvested allantoic fluid, confirming that vaccine-induced antibodies recognize shared antigenic epitopes across distinct H6 lineages. The investigators identified key study limitations, including the lack of quantitative in vitro receptor-binding assays, the absence of aerosol droplet transmission experiments, the reliance on a single field isolate, and the need for vaccine efficacy validation under commercial field conditions with secondary pathogens. Nonetheless, the investigation underscores that the continuous genetic exchange between waterfowl-origin surface glycoproteins and the robust H9N2 G57 internal ribonucleoprotein machinery produces resilient reassortants capable of threatening commercial poultry health, highlighting the urgent need for sustained poultry genomic surveillance. analysis.time: The outbreak was reported in December 2025, with the news article published on November 23, 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak occurred in Shangqiu, Henan Province, China, affecting a commercial layer flock of fifty-four-week-old chickens.
analysis.event: A novel reassortant avian influenza virus, designated A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, was identified and characterized in a poultry outbreak in central China. This virus belongs to the low-pathogenic H6N2 subtype but carries an unusual genetic composition combining segments from different avian influenza lineages.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak caused a fifteen percent cumulative mortality rate in the affected flock. The virus was confirmed as low-pathogenic, lacking the consecutive basic amino acids typical of highly pathogenic strains. However, it exhibited virulence markers in the neuraminidase and other proteins that could potentially enhance its pathogenicity in mammalian hosts.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The investigation involved whole-genome sequencing, postmortem examinations, and experimental inoculation of specific-pathogen-free chickens. The findings suggest the virus did not acquire internal segments through genetic drift but inherited an intact ribonucleoprotein cassette. However, the study had limitations, including the absence of in vitro receptor-binding assays and aerosol transmission experiments.

analysis.brief_en: A novel avian influenza reassortant virus, A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, was identified in a poultry outbreak in Shangqiu, Henan Province, China, in December 2025. This low-pathogenic H6N2 subtype combines genetic segments from different avian influenza lineages, including the hemagglutinin gene from a waterfowl-origin H6 lineage and the neuraminidase gene from an H9N2 poultry lineage. The outbreak resulted in a 15% mortality rate in the affected flock, with severe respiratory symptoms and signs of yolk sac peritonitis. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that the internal gene segments were inherited from the H9N2 G57 genotype, which is common in terrestrial poultry. Experimental studies showed that specific-pathogen-free chickens inoculated with the virus survived without overt clinical symptoms, but microscopic analysis revealed extensive tissue damage. The study highlights the potential for genetic reassortment between wild and domestic birds, raising concerns about the virus's adaptability and the need for continued genomic surveillance in poultry populations.

news.title_zh: 在中国家禽中发现新型 禽流感 重配病毒 暴发 - Bioengineer.org
news.source_body_en: A novel avian influenza reassortant virus, A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, was identified in a poultry outbreak in Shangqiu, Henan Province, China, in December 2025. This low-pathogenic H6N2 subtype combines genetic segments from different avian influenza lineages, including the hemagglutinin gene from a waterfowl-origin H6 lineage and the neuraminidase gene from an H9N2 poultry lineage. The outbreak resulted in a 15% mortality rate in the affected flock, with severe respiratory symptoms and signs of yolk sac peritonitis. Whole-genome sequencing revealed that the internal gene segments were inherited from the H9N2 G57 genotype, which is common in terrestrial poultry. Experimental studies showed that specific-pathogen-free chickens inoculated with the virus survived without overt clinical symptoms, but microscopic analysis revealed extensive tissue damage. The study highlights the potential for genetic reassortment between wild and domestic birds, raising concerns about the virus's adaptability and the need for continued genomic surveillance in poultry populations.
news.content_zh: 2025 年 12 月,在中国河南省商丘市的家禽 暴发 中鉴定出一种新型 禽流感 重配病毒 A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025。这种低致病性 H6N2 亚型结合了来自不同 禽流感 谱系的遗传片段,包括来自水禽起源的 H6 谱系的血凝素基因和来自 H9N2 家禽谱系的神经氨酸酶基因。暴发 导致受影响鸡群的 死亡率 发病率为 15%,出现严重的呼吸道症状和卵黄囊腹膜炎体征。全基因组测序显示,内部基因片段继承自H9N2 G57基因型,该基因型在陆生家禽中很常见。实验研究表明,接种该病毒的无特定病原体的鸡能够存活,没有明显的临床症状,但显微镜分析显示存在广泛的组织损伤。该研究强调了野生鸟类和家养鸟类之间遗传重配的可能性,引发了人们对该病毒的适应性以及在家禽种群中持续进行 基因组监测 的需求的担忧。
news.summary_zh: 2025 年 12 月,在中国河南省商丘市的家禽 暴发 中鉴定出一种新型 禽流感 重配病毒 A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025。这种低致病性 H6N2 亚型结合了来自不同 禽流感 谱系的遗传片段,包括来自水禽起源的 H6 谱系的血凝素基因和来自 H9N2 家禽谱系的神经氨酸酶基因。暴发 导致受影响鸡群的 死亡率 发病率为 15%,出现严重的呼吸道症状和卵黄囊腹膜炎体征。全基因组测序显示,内部基因片段继承自H9N2 G57基因型,该基因型在陆生家禽中很常见。实验研究表明,接种该病毒的无特定病原体的鸡能够存活,没有明显的临床症状,但显微镜分析显示存在广泛的组织损伤。该研究强调了野生鸟类和家养鸟类之间遗传重配的可能性,引发了人们对该病毒的适应性以及在家禽种群中持续进行 基因组监测 的需求的担忧。

Murphy) Advertisment17 Share Tweet China has reported a human case of H5N1 bird flu in a man who lives in Vietnam and regularly crosses the border for business, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). The source of his infection is unclear. The man, who lives in Quang Ninh province in northern Vietnam, developed symptoms on Nov. 1. He had a cough, nasal congestion and a runny nose when he was screened the next day at Dongxing Port, a border crossing in China’s Guangxi region. A sample taken at the crossing tested positive for H5N1 in China, while later samples collected in Vietnam tested negative. By Nov. 4, the man was in stable condition with no fever, cough or difficulty breathing. China reported the case to the WHO between Nov. 13 and 19. Health officials found no known exposure to poultry, other potentially infected animals or contaminated environments. Article continues below the player Two people in the man’s household in Vietnam had no symptoms and tested negative for influenza A, including the H5 subtype. No additional cases have been reported in connection with the case. The WHO’s Western Pacific region has recorded five human H5N1 cases and one death so far in 2026. Since 2020, the region has recorded 48 cases and 18 deaths. That includes 23 cases and eight deaths from 2020 through 2024 and 20 cases and nine deaths in 2025. BNO News learned of the WHO report through Avian Flu Diary. Murphy) Advertisment17 Share Tweet China has reported a human case of H5N1 bird flu in a man who lives in Vietnam and regularly crosses the border for business, according to the World Health Organization (WHO). The source of his infection is unclear. The man, who lives in Quang Ninh province in northern Vietnam, developed symptoms on Nov. 1. He had a cough, nasal congestion and a runny nose when he was screened the next day at Dongxing Port, a border crossing in China’s Guangxi region. A sample taken at the crossing tested positive for H5N1 in China, while later samples collected in Vietnam tested negative. By Nov. 4, the man was in stable condition with no fever, cough or difficulty breathing. China reported the case to the WHO between Nov. 13 and 19. Health officials found no known exposure to poultry, other potentially infected animals or contaminated environments. Article continues below the player Two people in the man’s household in Vietnam had no symptoms and tested negative for influenza A, including the H5 subtype. No additional cases have been reported in connection with the case. The WHO’s Western Pacific region has recorded five human H5N1 cases and one death so far in 2026. Since 2020, the region has recorded 48 cases and 18 deaths. That includes 23 cases and eight deaths from 2020 through 2024 and 20 cases and nine deaths in 2025. BNO News learned of the WHO report through Avian Flu Diary. news.content_zh: 据世界卫生组织 (WHO) 称,中国报告了一名来自越南的旅客感染 H5N1 禽流感病例。该男子居住在广宁省,于2026年11月4日出现症状,并在中国广西东兴口岸接受筛查。在港口采集的样本检测结果呈 H5N1 阳性,而后来在越南的检测结果呈阴性。该男子目前情况稳定,没有发烧、咳嗽或呼吸困难。他的感染源尚不清楚,卫生官员没有发现已知的家禽接触史或受污染的环境。尚未报告与此案件相关的其他案件。世界卫生组织西太平洋地区在 2026 年记录了 5 例人类 H5N1 病例和 1 例死亡,自 2020 年以来已出现 48 例病例和 18 例死亡。该病例凸显了该地区持续存在的 H5N1 禽流感风险,但没有提供有关应对或遏制措施的进一步细节。

analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: 587 bird deaths reported in an outbreak, with the remainder of the flock (18,723 birds) culled. The outbreak is associated with H5N1, which is a highly pathogenic avian influenza subtype. No human infections or specific risk levels were mentioned.

analysis.brief_en: Poland has reported its first bird flu outbreak in six months, according to The Poultry Site. The outbreak, identified as H5N1, occurred on a turkey farm where 587 out of 18,723 birds died, and the remaining flock was culled. The report was published on 24 November 2026, and the source is a syndicated summary, meaning the full original article body was not reviewed. The outbreak highlights the ongoing risks of avian influenza in poultry populations, but no specific details on testing, isolation, or contact tracing were provided. The Poultry Site is a reputable source in the poultry industry, and the report underscores the need for continued vigilance and biosecurity measures to prevent the spread of H5N1. This event is part of a broader context of avian influenza monitoring and response efforts across Europe and other regions.

news.content: Menu English हिन्दी Categories India Business Politics Sports Technology Startups Entertainment Hatke International Automobile Science Travel Miscellaneous Fashion Education Health & Fitness For the best experience use inshorts app on your smartphone WHO confirms three human H5N1 bird flu cases, one death in US short / 02:48 pm on Wednesday, 25 November 2026 The World Health Organization (WHO) has confirmed three human cases of H5N1 bird flu in Washington, US, including one death. All three individuals worked on dairy farms where cattle tested positive for the virus. WHO maintains that the risk to the general public remains low, while occupational exposure poses a low to moderate risk. read more at Medical Dialogues Shah Rukh Khan dances to 'Lungi Dance', delivers 'Om Shanti Om' dialogue at Udaipur wedding short by Anmol Sharma / 07:06 am on Friday, 27 November 2026 Actor Shah Rukh Khan performed at a private wedding in Udaipur, with several videos from the event surfacing online. The 61-year-old danced to 'Lungi Dance' from 'Chennai Express' and delivered his famous 'Itni shiddat se' dialogue from 'Om Shanti Om'. He also surprised the groom by recreating his signature pose behind him while singer Sonu Nigam performed on the stage. read more at Indian Express India A knocked out of Rising Stars Asia Cup short by Anmol Sharma / 10:47 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 Sri Lanka A defeated India A by eight wickets in the first semi-final of the Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 in Qatar's Doha. Batting first, India A posted a total of 317/8, with opener Abhishek Sharma top-scoring with 78(63), while Shahbaz Ahmed scored 54*(48). Sri Lanka chased down the target in 41.3 overs, with both their openers slamming tons. read more at Cricinfo World record for highest score by number 11 batter in T20 cricket broken short by Anmol Sharma / 08:45 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 India pacer Jaydev Unadkat on Thursday broke the world record for the highest score by a number 11 batter in men's T20 cricket history. Unadkat smashed 40 runs off 26 balls for Saurashtra against Tamil Nadu in Indore, hitting three fours and two sixes. The previous record was held by Danny Briggs, who scored 35*(18) for Adelaide Strikers in 2020. read more at Cricinfo Gold and silver prices jump in India short by Bhawana Chaudhary / 06:34 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 A day after witnessing a massive dip, the prices of gold and silver jumped sharply on Thursday. Gold got expensive by ₹1,603 and hit ₹1,22,641 per 10 grams, as per IBJA data. Silver too jumped by ₹4,402 to close at ₹1,47,347 per kilogram on Thursday. On Wednesday, gold and silver were down ₹3,907 per 10 g and ₹9,680/kg, respectively. read more at IBJA What financial changes will come into effect in December? short by Anmol Sharma / 06:00 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 Several financial changes take effect from December 1. SBI Card will levy a 1% fee on transport transactions above ₹30,000 and on fuel spending exceeding ₹50,000 in a billing cycle. SEBI's new commodity derivatives margins of 6-10% begin. RBI will review interest rates from December 2-4, while Aadhaar email updates remain free till December 31. LPG prices may be revised. read more at News18 Which stocks could be impacted if US imposes 25% tariffs on India? short by Mansi Agarwal / 05:12 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 Proposed US tariffs of 25% on India could affect export-oriented stocks, particularly in textiles, seafood, chemicals, gems and jewellery. Pearl Global and Welspun Living may face pressure, while Apex Frozen Foods and Avanti Feeds could be hit as higher duties make Indian shrimp less competitive. Domestic sectors such as banking and power may prove more resilient. read more at Livemint WhatsApp users can now schedule messages short by Bhawana Chaudhary / 03:43 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 WhatsApp has rolled out its most-awaited 'scheduled messages' feature, allowing users to write messages in advance and send them on their preferred date and time. Users can send messages anywhere from 10 minutes to 14 days later, in both 1:1 and group chats. Messages can be scheduled by pressing and holding the 'Send' button, before picking the date and time. read more at News18 Massive explosion at Bangkok oil depot short by Daisy Mowke / 03:09 pm on Thursday, 26 November 2026 An explosion occurred at Bangchak oil depot in Bangkok on Thursday, triggering a massive fire and sending thick black smoke into the sky. Authorities urged residents living near the facility to evacuate as a precaution. Emergency services responded to the incident, and the fire was reportedly brought under control. No casualties were immediately reported. read more at Hindustan Times Load More Your browser does not support JavaScript!

Health and agricultural authorities have issued a renewed warning after two dead wild swans in County Offaly tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu. The H5N1 virus was confirmed following ongoing surveillance of wild birds, highlighting the increasing threat to Ireland’s poultry industry. In response to the growing risk, a mandatory housing order for poultry and captive birds will take effect across Ireland on Monday, 23rd November 2026, requiring bird owners to prevent contact with wild birds. Minister for Agriculture Mr Martin Heydon has urged all poultry keepers, including small backyard flock owners, to strengthen biosecurity measures and remain alert for signs of infection. Public Health Advice: Members of the public are advised not to touch sick or dead wild birds and to report suspected cases through the Department of Agriculture’s Avian Check app. Health authorities currently consider the risk of H5N1 infection to the general public to be low. The latest detections serve as an important reminder of the need for continued vigilance to protect Ireland’s wild birds and poultry sector. Health and agricultural authorities have issued a renewed warning after two dead wild swans in County Offaly tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu. The H5N1 virus was confirmed following ongoing surveillance of wild birds, highlighting the increasing threat to Ireland’s poultry industry. In response to the growing risk, a mandatory housing order for poultry and captive birds will take effect across Ireland on Monday, 23rd November 2026, requiring bird owners to prevent contact with wild birds. Minister for Agriculture Mr Martin Heydon has urged all poultry keepers, including small backyard flock owners, to strengthen biosecurity measures and remain alert for signs of infection. Public Health Advice: Members of the public are advised not to touch sick or dead wild birds and to report suspected cases through the Department of Agriculture’s Avian Check app. Health authorities currently consider the risk of H5N1 infection to the general public to be low. The latest detections serve as an important reminder of the need for continued vigilance to protect Ireland’s wild birds and poultry sector. news.content_title: WHO Reports Three H5N1 Infections In US Dairy Workers, One Death
news.content: ON NOW Arise 360 13:02, 25th Nov, 2026 by AriseNews WHO Reports Three H5N1 Infections In US Dairy Workers, One Death Global H5N1 infections occurred among farm workers exposed to infected cattle, while the global health agency says the risk to the general population remains low. Follow ARISE News on GoogleAdd us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google Follow us on Google The World Health Organisation (WHO) has reported three human infections involving the H5N1 strain of avian influenza in Washington State, United States, including one death among workers exposed to infected dairy cattle. In a disease outbreak update published on Tuesday, November 24, the organisation said the United States had notified it of three laboratory-confirmed infections identified between October 16 and November 4. All three patients were adults who worked on dairy cattle farms in Yakima County, where the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus had been detected among cattle. The first patient developed symptoms including eye irritation, a runny nose, muscle aches and headaches in early October. The individual sought medical attention and was not hospitalised. The second patient developed respiratory symptoms and later required hospital treatment for severe illness. The patient died on November 1, making the case the first reported death following exposure to infected dairy cattle or a related contaminated environment. Related News: Colorado Confirms Four Cases Of H5N1 Bird Flu Philippines Confirms Two New Mpox Cases, Raising Active Infections To Three UK Tops 50,000 Coronavirus Deaths as Italy Reaches One Million Infections The third patient developed conjunctivitis, an inflammation of the eye, but did not require hospitalisation. Laboratory testing and subsequent genetic analysis confirmed that the infections involved the H5N1 virus. The WHO said the viruses were highly similar to those detected in dairy cattle in Washington State, supporting the assessment that the infections resulted from exposure to infected animals or contaminated environments. The organisation said investigations and monitoring of people exposed to the affected cattle, as well as close contacts of the patients, were ongoing. However, it stressed that there was no evidence of human-to-human transmission associated with the three cases. Based on available information, the WHO assessed the risk posed by H5N1 to the general population as low. It said the risk was considered low to moderate for people with occupational exposure to infected animals. The latest cases add to the number of human infections reported in the United States since the country began documenting the outbreak. According to the WHO, 75 human infections involving influenza A(H5) viruses had been reported in the country since 2024, including the three cases covered in its latest update. Avian influenza viruses primarily circulate among birds and other animals but can occasionally infect humans following direct exposure to infected animals or contaminated environments. The WHO continues to monitor the outbreak and has called for surveillance, laboratory testing and public health measures to limit further exposure. The organisation said the situation could change as investigations produce additional information. It also urged continued monitoring of people working with potentially infected animals, particularly in areas where outbreaks have been detected. The agency’s assessment indicates that the latest infections require public health attention, but there is currently no evidence that the virus is spreading between people. Catherine Okonkwo. news.content_original: ON NOW Arise 360 13:02, 25th Nov, 2026 by AriseNews WHO Reports Three H5N1 Infections In US Dairy Workers, One Death Global H5N1 infections occurred among farm workers exposed to infected cattle, while the global health agency says the risk to the general population remains low. Follow ARISE News on GoogleAdd us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google Follow us on Google The World Health Organisation (WHO) has reported three human infections involving the H5N1 strain of avian influenza in Washington State, United States, including one death among workers exposed to infected dairy cattle. In a disease outbreak update published on Tuesday, November 24, the organisation said the United States had notified it of three laboratory-confirmed infections identified between October 16 and November 4. All three patients were adults who worked on dairy cattle farms in Yakima County, where the highly pathogenic avian influenza virus had been detected among cattle. The first patient developed symptoms including eye irritation, a runny nose, muscle aches and headaches in early October. The individual sought medical attention and was not hospitalised. The second patient developed respiratory symptoms and later required hospital treatment for severe illness. The patient died on November 1, making the case the first reported death following exposure to infected dairy cattle or a related contaminated environment. Related News: Colorado Confirms Four Cases Of H5N1 Bird Flu Philippines Confirms Two New Mpox Cases, Raising Active Infections To Three UK Tops 50,000 Coronavirus Deaths as Italy Reaches One Million Infections The third patient developed conjunctivitis, an inflammation of the eye, but did not require hospitalisation. Laboratory testing and subsequent genetic analysis confirmed that the infections involved the H5N1 virus. The WHO said the viruses were highly similar to those detected in dairy cattle in Washington State, supporting the assessment that the infections resulted from exposure to infected animals or contaminated environments. The organisation said investigations and monitoring of people exposed to the affected cattle, as well as close contacts of the patients, were ongoing. However, it stressed that there was no evidence of human-to-human transmission associated with the three cases. Based on available information, the WHO assessed the risk posed by H5N1 to the general population as low. It said the risk was considered low to moderate for people with occupational exposure to infected animals. The latest cases add to the number of human infections reported in the United States since the country began documenting the outbreak. According to the WHO, 75 human infections involving influenza A(H5) viruses had been reported in the country since 2024, including the three cases covered in its latest update. Avian influenza viruses primarily circulate among birds and other animals but can occasionally infect humans following direct exposure to infected animals or contaminated environments. The WHO continues to monitor the outbreak and has called for surveillance, laboratory testing and public health measures to limit further exposure. The organisation said the situation could change as investigations produce additional information. It also urged continued monitoring of people working with potentially infected animals, particularly in areas where outbreaks have been detected. The agency’s assessment indicates that the latest infections require public health attention, but there is currently no evidence that the virus is spreading between people. Catherine Okonkwo. news.content: Avian Flu Diary Covering Pandemic and Seasonal Flu, Emerging Infectious Diseases, public health, community & Individual preparedness. NOTE: All AFD blogs are written by a human - any mistakes are solely mine. Thursday, November 26, 2026 Nature Comms: Protective effect of seasonal vaccines against human-derived bovine H5N1 influenza virus (translated) Credit University of Tokyo Press Release #19,430 Given the enormous logistics of creating, testing, manufacturing, and deploying a pandemic strain-specific vaccine (see Maggie Fox's SCI AM - A Bird Flu Vaccine Might Come Too Late to Save Us from H5N1), many researchers have looked for potential stop-gap benefits from seasonal flu vaccination. It's not a new idea (see 2008's Seasonal Flu Vaccine May Offer Some Protection To H5N1 and 2010's Seasonal influenza vaccine elicits heterosubtypic immunity against H5N1 that can be further boosted by H5N1 vaccination), but more recent studies have provided mixed and modest results at best. Some of those studies include: Nature Comms: Adjuvanted Influenza Vaccination Increases Pre-existing H5N1 Cross-reactive Antibodies mBio: Low levels of influenza H5N1 HA and NA antibodies in the human population are boosted by seasonal H1N1 infection but not by H3N2 infection or influenza vaccination EID Journal: Effect of Seasonal Influenza Vaccines on Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Clade 2.3.4.4b Virus Infection in Ferrets EID Journal: Investigation of Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Neutralization by Quadrivalent Seasonal Vaccines, United Kingdom, 2021–2024 Our most recent foray into this topic was last September's EM&I: Limited added benefit of seasonal influenza vaccination before A(H5) vaccination in mice and ferrets challenged with A(H5N1), which offered little encouragement on the effectiveness of using seasonal flu vaccines as a `prime-boost' for H5N1 vaccines. That said, there are known, or suspected, benefits to having been recently vaccinated against seasonal flu in the face of a pandemic strain. It still may provide some small boost to your immune response. HA neutralizing antibodies aren't the only immune defense against infection. The N1 component from H1N1 may provide some degree of protection against severe illness, although unlikely to prevent infection It could help prevent a co-infection with H5N1 and seasonal flu, which has the potential for being more severe. Co-infections could also help generate a reassorted `hybrid' virus (see Preprint: Intelligent Prediction & Biological Validation of the High Reassortment Potential of Avian H5N1 and Human H3N2 Influenza Viruses). Today, we've a study out of the University of Tokyo led by Yoshihiro Kawaoka and Professor Ryuta Uraki, that introduces a new wrinkle. Instead of only testing the standard quadrivalent flu shot (inactivated influenza vaccine), it adds a trivalent live-attenuated influenza vaccine (LAIV; FluMist) to the mix. Flumist is currently only available for those aged 2-49 in the United States, and carries a number of exclusions, including pregnant women, immunocompromised individuals, or those who have recently received antiviral medications. As the graphic at the top of this blog indicates, those lab animals who received the live-attenuated influenza vaccine fared far better (83% survival vs 0%) than those which were inoculated with the standard flu shot. From the press release: When the immune responses involved in these protective effects were examined, no neutralizing antibodies against bovine-derived H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus were detected with any of the vaccines. On the other hand, the nasal attenuated live vaccine induced a stronger T-cell response to the virus than the inactivated vaccine. These results suggest that the nasal attenuated live vaccine also shows protective effects against bovine-derived H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza virus, and that this effect may be related to an immune response involving T cells. However, these results are based on animal experiments using ferrets and do not directly indicate infection prevention or severity prevention effects in humans. While an intriguing finding, there are a lot of caveats to consider, including: This was a small study using one H5N1 strain and a limited number of flu-naive ferrets. While useful in flu research, ferrets are not a perfect analog for humans, which invariably have a lengthy and messy history of exposures to influenza A viruses and/or vaccines. That said, there are known, or suspected, benefits to having been recently vaccinated against seasonal flu in the face of a pandemic strain. It still may provide some small boost to your immune response. HA neutralizing antibodies aren't the only immune defense against infection. The N1 component from H1N1 may provide some degree of protection against severe illness, although unlikely to prevent infection It could help prevent a co-infection with H5N1 and seasonal flu, which has the potential for being more severe. Co-infections could also help generate a reassorted `hybrid' virus (see Preprint: Intelligent Prediction & Biological Validation of the High Reassortment Potential of Avian H5N1 and Human H3N2 Influenza Viruses). Today, we've a study out of the University of Tokyo led by Yoshihiro Kawaoka and Professor Ryuta Uraki, that introduces a new wrinkle. Of course, additional research might pave the way for LAIVs limited use in a future pandemic crisis. That said, it is a fascinating study, which many will want to read in its entirety. The study found that live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV) induced stronger T-cell responses and provided substantial protection against lethal infection, while inactivated vaccines only reduced viral replication and delayed disease progression.
elements_en.scale_impact_and_risk: Two human cases of H5N1 infection were reported in Washington State, with one fatality. The virus has caused outbreaks in 44 infected herds since early October 2024. The study involved influenza-naïve female ferrets, with 5 out of 6 surviving after LAIV vaccination and 0 surviving after inactivated vaccine.
elements_en.response_status_and_uncertainty: The study was conducted on ferrets and does not directly indicate infection prevention or severity prevention effects in humans. The Washington State Public Health Laboratory tested specimens using CDC influenza A(H5) assay. Close contacts of confirmed cases are being monitored, but details on the number and type of contacts are not available.

news.source_body_en: The Avian Flu Diary reports on a study from the University of Tokyo, published on November 25, 2026, which evaluated the protective effects of seasonal influenza vaccines against a human-derived bovine H5N1 virus in ferrets. The study found that live attenuated influenza vaccines (LAIV) induced stronger T-cell responses and provided substantial protection against lethal infection, while inactivated vaccines only reduced viral replication and delayed disease progression. In Washington State, nearly 6 weeks prior, the first dairy-cattle associated human infection with H5N1 was reported in Yakima County, followed by two more cases, one of which was fatal. The virus has caused outbreaks in 44 herds since early October 2024. The study involved influenza-naïve female ferrets, with 5 out of 6 surviving after LAIV vaccination and 0 surviving after inactivated vaccine. Close contacts of confirmed cases are being monitored, but details on the number and type of contacts are not available. The findings suggest that immune responses beyond serum antibodies, including cellular and potentially mucosal immunity, may contribute to cross-protection against antigenically distinct bovine-derived H5N1 viruses. However, these results are based on animal experiments and do not directly indicate effects in humans.

Topics & Projects Antimicrobial Stewardship Chronic Wasting Disease Osterholm Update Podcasts Newsletters About CIDRAP CIDRAP in the News Our Staff Our Director Osterholm in the Press Shop Merchandise Contact Us About Search CLOSE Search Support Menu Uptick in H5N1 avian flu activity continues across North America News brief Stephanie Soucheray, MA Topics Avian Influenza (Bird Flu) Share Copied to clipboard Addison Berry/Flickr cc Avian flu activity continues to rise across the nation, with two more detections noted in dairy cattle herds this week, one each in Texas and Washington state. In the past 30 days, 26 cattle detections have been noted in dairy herds by the US Department of Agriculture’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS). Of the 26 detections, 17 have been in Washington state, with high activity in major dairy operations in the Yakima Valley. This week the World Health Organization detailed three human H5N1 cases reported in Yakima Valley in October and November, stating that all three patients were adults who worked on dairy cattle farms. No cases involved person-to-person transmission, and the report does not say if infected people all worked on the same farm. One of the case-patients (who had underlying health problems) died from the infection and was the first death reported globally following exposure to infected dairy cattle. The other two patients had mild illness, with conjunctivitis as an initial symptom. Zoo outbreak kills spider monkey, tigrillo In commercial poultry news, five new operations have reported H5N1 outbreaks this week, including a commercial broiler production in Sussex County, Delaware, affecting 269,900 birds. In the past 30 days, 4.02 million birds have been hit with avian flu in 32 US flocks, including 10 commercial and 22 backyard flocks, according to APHIS data. Finally in international news, Mexican health authorities announced the immediate closure of the Leon Municipal Zoo in the state of Guanajuato following an outbreak of H5N1. On November 16, the zoo noted the virus in dead migratory waterfowl found in the zoo’s central lake. Yesterday, testing showed H5N1 infection in two dead captive animals: a tigrillo (a small member of the cat family; see photo above) and a spider monkey, with a second spider monkey showing symptoms. The zoo is closed for the next five days. Nonmedical measles vaccine exemptions for kindergarteners tied to 16% higher risk of outbreaks News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Measles Childhood Vaccines NIH Higher rates of nonmedical measles-vaccine exemptions for school entry were associated with a 16% higher outbreak likelihood in a study representing 237 million people in 30 US states. For the study, published yesterday in JAMA Network Open, a team led by a University of Washington researcher analyzed measles cases reported by the Johns Hopkins University Measles Tracker in 2025, state- and county-level data on measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine coverage among kindergarteners, and vaccine exemptions. The outbreak proxy was at least three measles cases per county, a count threshold rather than per-capita incidence; counties below that level were retained. The threshold didn’t establish epidemiologic linkage. The secondary outcome consisted of total county cases in counties with at least three cases rather than cases per outbreak. “Measles is among the most transmissible human pathogens, so even small, geographically clustered immunity gaps can sustain local transmission,” the authors wrote. “As aggregate national and state measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage can obscure this local susceptibility, pockets of unvaccinated persons may persist even where aggregate coverage appears adequate.” Findings may guide school preparedness The analytic sample represented 71.6% of the US population, and 1,821 of 2,214 (82.2%) counties reported measles cases in 2025; 3.4% met the proxy. Average MMR coverage was 91.1%, and the average nonmedical exemption rate was 4.6%. Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness. The joint model showed a link between greater exemption rates and outbreak occurrence (odds ratio [OR], 1.16) but no association for MMR uptake (OR, 1.01). In the exploratory burden model, the incidence rate ratio was 1.08. Higher exemption rates were tied to lower MMR coverage. Joint-model ORs were 1.12 to 1.17 using alternative thresholds. Burden estimates remained positive but were less consistent in sensitivity analyses, with wide confidence intervals that indicated imprecision. The relationship between school nonmedical exemption rates and a higher likelihood of measles outbreaks may reflect clustering of susceptibility, differential measurement error in uptake and exemption data, or both, the authors said. “Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness,” they concluded. Higher HPV viral loads tied to increased risk of cervical cancer News brief Meghan Holohan Topics Human Papillomavirus (HPV) ronnachaipark / iStock Most people will experience a human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in their lifetime. High-risk strains of HPV cause cervical cancer in women, the fourth most common cancer in women worldwide. A paper published this week in the journal Cancer finds that viral load contributes to why some people develop cervical cancer, and others don’t. “Two women with similar HPV viral loads at one visit may have very different outcomes depending on how those levels change over time,” said co-corresponding author Lina Zhang, MD, in a news release from Wiley, the publisher of the journal. “Our findings suggest that a rising or persistently high viral load may signal a greater likelihood of cervical lesions.” Findings could lead to better monitoring Zhang and her colleagues at Nanjing Medical University in China led the study, which tracked 624 women (53.3%) who had persistent HPV infection, 471 (40.3%) who cleared their HPV infection, and 75 (6.4%) with a reactivated infection. Women with lingering HPV infections had higher viral loads than those who cleared it or had HPV reactivation. Those with moderate increasing or persistently high viral loads were more likely to develop cervical cancer than those with low stable or moderate declining viral loads. In total, 11% of women with low stable viral loads, 18% of women with moderate declining trajectories, 74% with moderately increasing viral loads, and 90% with persistently high viral loads had precancerous cervical lesions. Two women with similar HPV viral loads at one visit may have very different outcomes depending on how those levels change over time. Lina Zhang, MD Considering viral load could help doctors understand a woman’s future risk and create better surveillance plans for them. “We hope these findings will contribute to more personalized follow-up strategies and ultimately improve cervical disease prevention,” said co–corresponding author Zhonghua Shi, MD, in the release. Point-of-care test for syphilis receives emergency use authorization News brief Chris Dall, MA Topics Sexually Transmitted Infections Diagnostics quantic69 / iStock The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued emergency use authorization for a point-of-care molecular test for active syphilis, and three other pathogens that cause sexually transmitted infections (STIs). The test, developed by Roche Diagnostics, can detect Treponema pallidum—the bacterium that causes syphilis—from a single lesion swab sample within 15 minutes. It can also detect mpox virus and herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2. The three STIs can cause similar symptoms but require different treatments. Officials with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which helped speed the review of the test through its Rapid Acceleration of Diagnostics Tech Independent Test Assessment Program, say the point-of-care test can help healthcare providers identify active syphilis infection and initiate appropriate treatment more quickly. “Point-of-care testing leads to faster treatment in the same visit, thus reducing transmission and worsening illness,” Bruce Tromberg, PhD, director of NIH’s National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, said in an agency press release. Rise in syphilis cases It’s the first point-of-care test for syphilis to receive FDA authorization. Current syphilis diagnosis relies on blood-based serologic tests. US syphilis cases have risen by 42% since 2020, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with 190,242 cases reported in 2024. Cases of congenital syphilis—the transfer of the infection from the mother to the fetus—have risen by 82%. If left untreated, syphilis can cause serious heart and brain damage, blindness, deafness, and paralysis. Congenital syphilis can lead to miscarriage, infant death, and lifelong medical issues. NIH says the test will become available in the United States in the coming months. RSV shots safe for older adults, alone or in combo, analysis finds News brief Liz Szabo, MA Topics Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Adult (non-flu) Vaccines lucigerma / iStock Multiple clinical trials have found that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines are safe in adults. Now, a new study in people age 60 and older shows it’s also safe to receive an RSV shot plus another vaccine in the same week. In a study of 18,252 people published this week in Vaccine, less than 1% of participants reported seeking medical attention during the week after being vaccinated against RSV. The study was based on reports to V-safe, a voluntary registry run by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that allows people to report side effects or other problems after receiving a vaccine. About one-third of people reported a mild or moderate health issue within a week after getting an RSV shot, including a sore arm, fatigue, muscle ache, and headache. About one in three people vaccinated against RSV received another vaccine within a week, according to the study, led by CDC scientists. Side effects differ by vaccine manufacturer People given the RSV vaccine made by Pfizer (Abrysvo) plus another shot were more likely to report side effects around the injection site compared with people who received the Pfizer shot alone. Study participants who received GSK’s RSV vaccine (Arexvy), either alone or with another vaccine, were more likely to report symptoms than those who received the Pfizer vaccine. Those who received the Moderna RSV vaccine (mResvia) had a similar risk of side effects as those given the Pfizer shot. The CDC recommends that people age 75 and older receive a single RSV shot. People older than 60 may also get an RSV vaccine if they are at high risk of developing severe disease from the illness. CWD digest: Fatal disease found on deer farms in Michigan, Kentucky News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Chronic Wasting Disease Larry Smith / Flickr cc Michigan: The Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development (MDARD) has confirmed the first-time detection of chronic wasting disease (CWD) in a cervid on a Roscommon County farm. While the type of cervid wasn’t identified in the news release, the farm raises game animals such as deer, elk, and reindeer, per media reports. Roscommon County, in the north-central part of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula, borders CWD-positive Ogemaw and Gladwin counties. “The presence of CWD in farmed cervid facilities is not new to Michigan; prior to this detection, cases have been found across multiple counties, including Calhoun, Hillsdale, Kent, Lake, Mackinac, Mecosta, Montcalm, Newaygo, and Osceola counties,” MDARD said. CWD is transmitted through infectious misfolded proteins called prions, which spread from animal to animal or through environmental contamination. Kentucky: A Shelby County deer farm is under quarantine after a deer tested positive for CWD last week—the first case in the county, the Kentucky Department of Agriculture reports. Shelby County is in the north-central part of the state and doesn’t border any CWD-positive county. “The Office of State Veterinarian established a management (5 mile radius) and surveillance (15 mile radius) zone for herds near the affected deer farm” and “is diligently reviewing recent movement records, and all deer farms in the management and surveillance zones are under restricted movement until further order of the State Veterinarian,” the news release said. The secondary outcome consisted of total county cases in counties with at least three cases rather than cases per outbreak. “Measles is among the most transmissible human pathogens, so even small, geographically clustered immunity gaps can sustain local transmission,” the authors wrote. “As aggregate national and state measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) coverage can obscure this local susceptibility, pockets of unvaccinated persons may persist even where aggregate coverage appears adequate.” Findings may guide school preparedness The analytic sample represented 71.6% of the US population, and 1,821 of 2,214 (82.2%) counties reported measles cases in 2025; 3.4% met the proxy. Average MMR coverage was 91.1%, and the average nonmedical exemption rate was 4.6%. Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness. The joint model showed a link between greater exemption rates and outbreak occurrence (odds ratio [OR], 1.16) but no association for MMR uptake (OR, 1.01). In the exploratory burden model, the incidence rate ratio was 1.08. Higher exemption rates were tied to lower MMR coverage. Joint-model ORs were 1.12 to 1.17 using alternative thresholds. Burden estimates remained positive but were less consistent in sensitivity analyses, with wide confidence intervals that indicated imprecision. The relationship between school nonmedical exemption rates and a higher likelihood of measles outbreaks may reflect clustering of susceptibility, differential measurement error in uptake and exemption data, or both, the authors said. “Routinely collected exemption data may complement local knowledge when prioritizing school-level review and preparedness,” they concluded. Higher HPV viral loads tied to increased risk of cervical cancer News brief Meghan Holohan Topics Human Papillomavirus (HPV) ronnachaipark / iStock Most people will experience a human papillomavirus (HPV) infection in their lifetime. High-risk strains of HPV cause cervical cancer in women, the fourth most common cancer in women worldwide. A paper published this week in the journal Cancer finds that viral load contributes to why some people develop cervical cancer, and others don’t. “Two women with similar HPV viral loads at one visit may have very different outcomes depending on how those levels change over time,” said co-corresponding author Lina Zhang, MD, in a news release from Wiley, the publisher of the journal. “Our findings suggest that a rising or persistently high viral load may signal a greater likelihood of cervical lesions.” Findings could lead to better monitoring Zhang and her colleagues at Nanjing Medical University in China led the study, which tracked 624 women (53.3%) who had persistent HPV infection, 471 (40.3%) who cleared their HPV infection, and 75 (6.4%) with a reactivated infection. Women with lingering HPV infections had higher viral loads than those who cleared it or had HPV reactivation. Those with moderate increasing or persistently high viral loads were more likely to develop cervical cancer than those with low stable or moderate declining viral loads. In total, 11% of women with low stable viral loads, 18% of women with moderate declining trajectories, 74% with moderately increasing viral loads, and 90% with persistently high viral loads had precancerous cervical lesions. Two women with similar HPV viral loads at one visit may have very different outcomes depending on how those levels change over time. Lina Zhang, MD Considering viral load could help doctors understand a woman’s future risk and create better surveillance plans for them. “We hope these findings will contribute to more personalized follow-up strategies and ultimately improve cervical disease prevention,” said co–corresponding author Zhonghua Shi, MD, in the release. Point-of-care test for syphilis receives emergency use authorization News brief Chris Dall, MA Topics Sexually Transmitted Infections Diagnostics quantic69 / iStock The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has issued emergency use authorization for a point-of-care molecular test for active syphilis, and three other pathogens that cause sexually transmitted infections (STIs). The test, developed by Roche Diagnostics, can detect Treponema pallidum—the bacterium that causes syphilis—from a single lesion swab sample within 15 minutes. It can also detect mpox virus and herpes simplex virus types 1 and 2. The three STIs can cause similar symptoms but require different treatments. Officials with the National Institutes of Health (NIH), which helped speed the review of the test through its Rapid Acceleration of Diagnostics Tech Independent Test Assessment Program, say the point-of-care test can help healthcare providers identify active syphilis infection and initiate appropriate treatment more quickly. “Point-of-care testing leads to faster treatment in the same visit, thus reducing transmission and worsening illness,” Bruce Tromberg, PhD, director of NIH’s National Institute of Biomedical Imaging and Bioengineering, said in an agency press release. Rise in syphilis cases It’s the first point-of-care test for syphilis to receive FDA authorization. Current syphilis diagnosis relies on blood-based serologic tests. US syphilis cases have risen by 42% since 2020, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, with 190,242 cases reported in 2024. Cases of congenital syphilis—the transfer of the infection from the mother to the fetus—have risen by 82%. If left untreated, syphilis can cause serious heart and brain damage, blindness, deafness, and paralysis. Congenital syphilis can lead to miscarriage, infant death, and lifelong medical issues. NIH says the test will become available in the United States in the coming months. RSV shots safe for older adults, alone or in combo, analysis finds News brief Liz Szabo, MA Topics Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV) Adult (non-flu) Vaccines lucigerma / iStock Multiple clinical trials have found that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines are safe in adults. Now, a new study in people age 60 and older shows it’s also safe to receive an RSV shot plus another vaccine in the same week. In a study of 18,252 people published this week in Vaccine, less than 1% of participants reported seeking medical attention during the week after being vaccinated against RSV. The study was based on reports to V-safe, a voluntary registry run by the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) that allows people to report side effects or other problems after receiving a vaccine. About one-third of people reported a mild or moderate health issue within a week after getting an RSV shot, including a sore arm, fatigue, muscle ache, and headache. About one in three people vaccinated against RSV received another vaccine within a week, according to the study, led by CDC scientists. Side effects differ by vaccine manufacturer People given the RSV vaccine made by Pfizer (Abrysvo) plus another shot were more likely to report side effects around the injection site compared with people who received the Pfizer shot alone. Study participants who received GSK’s RSV vaccine (Arexvy), either alone or with another vaccine, were more likely to report symptoms than those who received the Pfizer vaccine. Those who received the Moderna RSV vaccine (mResvia) had a similar risk of side effects as those given the Pfizer shot. The CDC recommends that people age 75 and older receive a single RSV shot. People older than 60 may also get an RSV vaccine if they are at high risk of developing severe disease from the illness. CWD digest: Fatal disease found on deer farms in Michigan, Kentucky News brief Mary Van Beusekom, MS Topics Chronic Wasting Disease Larry Smith / Flickr cc Michigan: The Michigan Department of Agriculture and Rural Development (MDARD) has confirmed the first-time detection of chronic wasting disease (CWD) in a cervid on a Roscommon County farm. While the type of cervid wasn’t identified in the news release, the farm raises game animals such as deer, elk, and reindeer, per media reports. Roscommon County, in the north-central part of Michigan’s Lower Peninsula, borders CWD-positive Ogemaw and Gladwin counties. “The presence of CWD in farmed cervid facilities is not new to Michigan; prior to this detection, cases have been found across multiple counties, including Calhoun, Hillsdale, Kent, Lake, Mackinac, Mecosta, Montcalm, Newaygo, and Osceola counties,” MDARD said. CWD is transmitted through infectious misfolded proteins called prions, which spread from animal to animal or through environmental contamination. Kentucky: A Shelby County deer farm is under quarantine after a deer tested positive for CWD last week—the first case in the county, the Kentucky Department of Agriculture reports. Shelby County is in the north-central part of the state and doesn’t border any CWD-positive county. “The Office of State Veterinarian established a management (5 mile radius) and surveillance (15 mile radius) zone for herds near the affected deer farm” and “is diligently reviewing recent movement records, and all deer farms in the management and surveillance zones are under restricted movement until further order of the State Veterinarian,” the news release said. news.title_original: Uptick in H5N1 avian flu activity continues across North America

analysis.time: The article was published on 2026-11-25. The event dates include October and November 2026 for human H5N1 cases, and November 16, 2026, for the zoo outbreak.
analysis.location_and_population: The outbreak is reported across North America, specifically in Washington state and Texas for cattle detections, and in the Leon Municipal Zoo in Guanajuato, Mexico, for the zoo outbreak. The affected population includes dairy cattle herds, captive animals, and humans working on dairy farms.
analysis.event: An uptick in H5N1 avian flu activity has been observed in North America, with detections in dairy cattle herds and human cases linked to exposure to infected cattle. A zoo outbreak in Mexico resulted in the death of a spider monkey and a tigrillo, with the zoo closed for five days.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: In the past 30 days, 26 cattle detections were reported in the US, with 17 in Washington state. Three human H5N1 cases were reported in Yakima Valley, with one death. The outbreak in the Leon Municipal Zoo affected multiple animals, and the risk of human-to-human transmission is not confirmed.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The World Health Organization reported human cases, and the US Department of Agriculture is monitoring cattle detections. The zoo has been closed for five days following the outbreak. The study on measles exemptions and H5N1 activity is not directly related to the avian flu event.

analysis.brief_en: The article reports an uptick in H5N1 avian flu activity across North America, with 26 detections in dairy cattle herds in the past 30 days, including 17 in Washington state. Three human cases of H5N1 were reported in Yakima Valley, October and November 2026, with one death linked to exposure to infected cattle. In Mexico, the Leon Municipal Zoo in Guanajuato closed after an H5N1 outbreak was confirmed in dead migratory waterfowl and two captive animals, a spider monkey and a tigrillo. The WHO noted no person-to-person transmission in the human cases. The US Department of Agriculture is tracking the spread, but the full extent of the outbreak and its impact on human health remain under investigation. The study on measles vaccine exemptions and outbreak likelihood is unrelated to the H5N1 activity described.

news.title: León Zoo temporarily closes after bird flu outbreak spreads to mammals

Home El Bajío El Bajío News León Zoo temporarily closes after bird flu outbreak spreads to mammals By MND Staff November 26, 2026 0 The León Zoo announced a 21-day closure after the deaths of two mammals that tested positive for avian influenza. (Sectur Guanajuato) The zoo in León, Guanajuato, temporarily closed its doors to the public this week amid an avian influenza outbreak that has killed birds and at least two mammals. Officials believe migratory birds may have introduced the virus to the zoo, located in the northeast of León, Guanajuato’s largest city. Zoo León announced its decision to close in a statement and a video message posted to social media. REFUERZA ZOOLEÓN MEDIDAS PREVENTIVAS ANTE PRESENCIA DE INFLUENZA AVIAR https://t.co/zKC7n8gmzK — Zooleon (@zooleon) November 25, 2026 “In accordance with the recommendations of both the federal Health Ministry and the state Health Ministry, we have taken the decision to temporarily close the León Zoo to the public starting Wednesday, Nov. 25,” the zoo’s director Diana Karen Casillas said on Tuesday. Casillas said that the decision to close the zoo is a “preventative measure” related to two cases of avian influenza (also known as bird flu) in mammals. Avian flu was confirmed in a spider monkey and a tigrillo (a small wild cat) that died at the zoo. The deaths of three geese, two wild ducks and a vulture at the zoo were reported earlier this month. Casillas said that the aim of the temporary closure — which is expected to last 21 days — is to “strengthen” measures aimed at stopping the spread of the disease. She said migratory birds brought avian flu to the zoo. “I want to stress that this situation is not exclusive to the León zoo,” Casillas said. “It can happen at any site that keeps wild animals,” she said. In its statement, Zoo León said that specialized zoo staff will continue feeding, monitoring and providing veterinary care to animals during the temporary closure. Casillas said in an interview that zoo personnel who work closely with animals use protective equipment. Fifteen workers developed flu-like symptoms after exposure to migratory birds with avian influenza, but to date none have tested positive for the disease, according to Guanajuato Health Minister Gabriel Cortéz Alcalá . The zoo thanked the public for its understanding during the temporary closure, and said that taking timely action is “essential to prevent infections, protect public health and safeguard animal life.” The zoo said its reopening will depend on how “the health situation” develops and on assessments by the relevant authorities. 2.3.4.4b分支)已在美国奶牛中引发疫情,并感染包括人类在内的其他哺乳动物。本研究评估了两种商用季节性流感疫苗对来源于人类的奶牛H5N1分离株A/Texas/37/2024在流感-na?ve(无免疫经验)雌性雪貂中的保护效力。所有未接种疫苗的雪貂均出现严重疾病,并因感染死亡或符合人道处死标准。接种灭活流感疫苗可降低多个呼吸道及肺外组织中的病毒滴度并延缓疾病进展,但无法防止致死性结局。相比之下,六只接种减毒活疫苗(Live Attenuated Influenza Vaccine,LAIV)的雪貂中有五只在攻毒后存活,并在鼻黏膜中表现出对病毒复制更有效的控制。减毒活疫苗接种诱导了更强的T细胞反应,而针对攻毒病毒未检测到中和活性,这提示保护性免疫可能依赖于细胞免疫而非中和抗体。这些研究结果表明,季节性减毒活流感疫苗接种可通过呼吸道细胞免疫应答,对一种抗原性不同的奶牛源H5N1病毒的致死性感染提供交叉保护。 自2024年初以来,高致病性禽流感(Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza,HPAI)H5N1病毒(clade 2.3.4.4b分支)在美国超过17个州的1,000余个奶牛群中持续流行,并发生由牛向包括人类在内的其他哺乳动物的传播事件,对公共卫生构成潜在威胁。研究人员此前报道,从人类病例中分离的奶牛源H5N1病毒A/Texas/37/2024可通过呼吸道飞沫在雪貂之间实现有效传播,凸显其跨种传播与持续致病的风险。当前常规使用的季节性流感疫苗所靶向的血凝素(Hemagglutinin,HA)抗原与流行奶牛H5N1病毒的H5 HA在抗原性上存在显著差异,但季节性疫苗诱导的神经氨酸酶(Neuraminidase,NA)交叉反应抗体以及针对核蛋白(Nucleoprotein,NP)等保守病毒蛋白的T细胞表位,可能提供一定程度的交叉保护。此外,经鼻内途径接种的减毒活疫苗(Live Attenuated Influenza Vaccine,LAIV)可诱导区别于肌肉注射灭活疫苗的黏膜免疫与细胞免疫应答。然而,上述交叉免疫反应能否有效抵御奶牛H5N1病毒的致死性感染,此前尚缺乏系统的实验证据。 瑞孚迪多肽药物研发解决方案>>领 取 为回答上述问题,研究人员在雪貂感染模型中评估了两种商用季节性流感疫苗——含Alhydrogel佐剂的四价灭活疫苗与三价减毒活疫苗FluMist——对人类来源奶牛H5N1分离株A/Texas/37/2024(hu-TX37-H5N1)的保护效力。研究团队通过监测临床疾病、存活时间、呼吸道与肺外器官病毒复制动态、组织病理学损伤、血清抗体应答谱及疫苗诱导的T细胞免疫水平,对两种疫苗平台的保护效果进行了多维度比较。该研究的结论对于H5N1禽流感大流行防范策略具有重要的现实意义:在特异性H5疫苗尚未广泛储备的情况下,现有季节性LAIV或可作为一种可快速动员的交叉保护手段。 研究人员采用的关键技术方法包括:基于已发表序列(EPI_ISL_19027114)利用反向遗传技术(reverse genetics)构建A/Texas/37/2024(H5N1)病毒;选用7至9月龄流感-na?ve雌性雪貂(经血清学确认对季节性流感A型和B型病毒阴性)为感染模型,实验方案获东京大学伦理委员会批准(批准号A2024PIA006-01);在生物安全三级(Biosafety Level 3,BSL-3)设施中完成活病毒攻毒;于第0天与第27天经肌肉注射进行两次免疫,间隔4周;采用血凝抑制试验(Hemagglutination Inhibition,HI)检测抗疫苗株抗体;采用聚焦减少中和试验(Focus Reduction Neutralization Test,FRNT)检测血清及鼻洗液中和活性;采用空斑试验(plaque assay)测定鼻拭子与器官病毒滴度;采用酶联免疫吸附试验(Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay,ELISA)检测HA、NA、NP结合抗体;采用神经氨酸酶抑制试验(Neuraminidase Inhibition Assay,NAI)评估NA抑制活性;采用酶联免疫斑点试验(Enzyme-linked Immunospot,ELISpot)检测外周血单个核细胞(Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells,PBMCs)中γ-干扰素(IFN-γ)分泌以评价T细胞应答。样本队列来源方面,四价灭活疫苗与三价减毒活疫苗(LAIV)购自Denka Seiken与Daiichi Sankyo,疫苗株由日本国立传染病研究所提供。 Seasonal influenza vaccination induces antibody responses against the vaccine strains(季节性流感疫苗接种诱导针对疫苗株的抗体应答):研究人员通过HI试验检测免疫后雪貂血清,结果显示接种灭活疫苗的雪貂针对三种疫苗株(A/Victoria/4897/2022(H1N1pdm)、A/California/122/2022(H3N2)及B/Austria/1359417/2021(B/Victoria系))的HI滴度总体高于接种LAIV的雪貂。 Live attenuated vaccination protects ferrets from lethal hu-TX37-H5N1 infection(减毒活疫苗接种保护雪貂抵抗致死性hu-TX37-H5N1感染):以100 PFU的hu-TX37-H5N1进行鼻内攻毒后,未接种组11只雪貂全部出现进行性体重下降及/或体温降低,并在8天内死亡或达到人道处死标准;接种灭活疫苗的雪貂同样发生严重疾病,全部在12天内死亡或被人道处死,但存活时间较未接种组明显延迟,表明灭活疫苗仅提供部分保护;而接种LAIV的6只雪貂中有5只存活攻毒,尽管部分动物出现短暂体重下降但大部分恢复,显示出LAIV在抗致死性感染方面优于灭活疫苗。 Live-attenuated vaccination limits viral replication in the nasal mucosa(减毒活疫苗接种限制鼻黏膜中的病毒复制):通过空斑试验检测鼻拭子样本,研究人员发现由于攻毒剂量较低(100 PFU),第1天未检测到病毒;第3天和第5天,两组疫苗接种组的病毒滴度均显著低于未接种组;攻毒后第7天,所有存活的灭活疫苗免疫雪貂中仍可检测到传染性病毒,而6只LAIV免疫雪貂中有4只未检测到病毒,且LAIV组病毒滴度显著低于灭活疫苗组,表明LAIV对鼻黏膜病毒复制的控制更为有效。 Inactivated vaccine and live attenuated vaccine reduce viral replication in organs(灭活疫苗和减毒活疫苗降低器官中的病毒复制):于攻毒后第3天采集每组4只雪貂的嗅球、脑、鼻甲、肺和气管组织进行病毒滴定,结果显示未接种组所有动物全部检测器官均检出病毒,两种疫苗均降低大多数器官的病毒滴度,但灭活疫苗组鼻甲的病毒滴度降低幅度有限;组织病理学检查显示未接种组肺部呈现肺泡炎,伴中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞浸润及浆液性渗出,严重者可见肺泡壁坏死,且坏死区域与流感病毒NP抗原检测阳性区域一致;灭活疫苗组病变严重程度个体差异较大;LAIV组总体肺泡病变更轻,病毒抗原检测多为阴性,提示LAIV对上呼吸道的病毒复制控制优于灭活疫苗。 Live attenuated vaccine induces a stronger cellular immune response than inactivated vaccine(减毒活疫苗诱导强于灭活疫苗的细胞免疫反应):研究人员未发现针对hu-TX37-H5N1的可检测中和抗体(血清及鼻洗液均为阴性);针对季节性疫苗株H1、H3及乙型HA的结合抗体滴度灭活疫苗组更高;针对H5N1的N1 NA和NP的交叉结合抗体也呈类似趋势;LAIV组血清可轻微但显著抑制N1蛋白活性,而灭活疫苗组无此活性;ELISpot检测显示LAIV诱导的针对H5N1 NP的T细胞反应(IFN-γ分泌)显著强于灭活疫苗。因此,保护性免疫可能与细胞免疫及可能的黏膜免疫相关,而非中和抗体。 研究人员在讨论中指出,两种疫苗均诱导针对疫苗株的免疫应答并降低病毒复制,但临床结局差异显著;保护差异无法用血清抗体解释,因灭活疫苗诱导了更高的HI滴度和结合抗体,而两组均未诱导针对hu-TX37-H5N1的中和抗体;LAIV的微弱NAI活性不足以单独解释其保护优势;LAIV诱导了更强的T细胞反应,识别NP等保守蛋白的T细胞可能交叉反应并与疾病缓解相关。研究亦存在局限:流感-na?ve雪貂两次接种不能完全模拟人类既有免疫;缺乏雪貂特异性试剂,无法充分评估呼吸道局部分泌型免疫应答;部分灭活疫苗组动物在攻毒后晚期死亡,死亡原因不明。 研究结论指出,季节性减毒活流感疫苗接种可为流感-na?ve雪貂提供针对致死性hu-TX37-H5N1感染的实质性保护,而灭活疫苗虽可降低病毒复制并延缓疾病进展,但无法预防死亡;保护性免疫可能依赖于血清抗体之外的细胞免疫及潜在黏膜免疫应答,为应对奶牛源H5N1病毒的交叉保护策略提供了实验依据。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2.3.4.4b分支)在美国超过17个州的1,000余个奶牛群中持续流行,并发生由牛向包括人类在内的其他哺乳动物的传播事件,对公共卫生构成潜在威胁。研究人员此前报道,从人类病例中分离的奶牛源H5N1病毒A/Texas/37/2024可通过呼吸道飞沫在雪貂之间实现有效传播,凸显其跨种传播与持续致病的风险。当前常规使用的季节性流感疫苗所靶向的血凝素(Hemagglutinin,HA)抗原与流行奶牛H5N1病毒的H5 HA在抗原性上存在显著差异,但季节性疫苗诱导的神经氨酸酶(Neuraminidase,NA)交叉反应抗体以及针对核蛋白(Nucleoprotein,NP)等保守病毒蛋白的T细胞表位,可能提供一定程度的交叉保护。此外,经鼻内途径接种的减毒活疫苗(Live Attenuated Influenza Vaccine,LAIV)可诱导区别于肌肉注射灭活疫苗的黏膜免疫与细胞免疫应答。然而,上述交叉免疫反应能否有效抵御奶牛H5N1病毒的致死性感染,此前尚缺乏系统的实验证据。 瑞孚迪多肽药物研发解决方案>>领 取 为回答上述问题,研究人员在雪貂感染模型中评估了两种商用季节性流感疫苗——含Alhydrogel佐剂的四价灭活疫苗与三价减毒活疫苗FluMist——对人类来源奶牛H5N1分离株A/Texas/37/2024(hu-TX37-H5N1)的保护效力。研究团队通过监测临床疾病、存活时间、呼吸道与肺外器官病毒复制动态、组织病理学损伤、血清抗体应答谱及疫苗诱导的T细胞免疫水平,对两种疫苗平台的保护效果进行了多维度比较。该研究的结论对于H5N1禽流感大流行防范策略具有重要的现实意义:在特异性H5疫苗尚未广泛储备的情况下,现有季节性LAIV或可作为一种可快速动员的交叉保护手段。 研究人员采用的关键技术方法包括:基于已发表序列(EPI_ISL_19027114)利用反向遗传技术(reverse genetics)构建A/Texas/37/2024(H5N1)病毒;选用7至9月龄流感-na?ve雌性雪貂(经血清学确认对季节性流感A型和B型病毒阴性)为感染模型,实验方案获东京大学伦理委员会批准(批准号A2024PIA006-01);在生物安全三级(Biosafety Level 3,BSL-3)设施中完成活病毒攻毒;于第0天与第27天经肌肉注射进行两次免疫,间隔4周;采用血凝抑制试验(Hemagglutination Inhibition,HI)检测抗疫苗株抗体;采用聚焦减少中和试验(Focus Reduction Neutralization Test,FRNT)检测血清及鼻洗液中和活性;采用空斑试验(plaque assay)测定鼻拭子与器官病毒滴度;采用酶联免疫吸附试验(Enzyme-linked Immunosorbent Assay,ELISA)检测HA、NA、NP结合抗体;采用神经氨酸酶抑制试验(Neuraminidase Inhibition Assay,NAI)评估NA抑制活性;采用酶联免疫斑点试验(Enzyme-linked Immunospot,ELISpot)检测外周血单个核细胞(Peripheral Blood Mononuclear Cells,PBMCs)中γ-干扰素(IFN-γ)分泌以评价T细胞应答。样本队列来源方面,四价灭活疫苗与三价减毒活疫苗(LAIV)购自Denka Seiken与Daiichi Sankyo,疫苗株由日本国立传染病研究所提供。 Seasonal influenza vaccination induces antibody responses against the vaccine strains(季节性流感疫苗接种诱导针对疫苗株的抗体应答):研究人员通过HI试验检测免疫后雪貂血清,结果显示接种灭活疫苗的雪貂针对三种疫苗株(A/Victoria/4897/2022(H1N1pdm)、A/California/122/2022(H3N2)及B/Austria/1359417/2021(B/Victoria系))的HI滴度总体高于接种LAIV的雪貂。 Live attenuated vaccination protects ferrets from lethal hu-TX37-H5N1 infection(减毒活疫苗接种保护雪貂抵抗致死性hu-TX37-H5N1感染):以100 PFU的hu-TX37-H5N1进行鼻内攻毒后,未接种组11只雪貂全部出现进行性体重下降及/或体温降低,并在8天内死亡或达到人道处死标准;接种灭活疫苗的雪貂同样发生严重疾病,全部在12天内死亡或被人道处死,但存活时间较未接种组明显延迟,表明灭活疫苗仅提供部分保护;而接种LAIV的6只雪貂中有5只存活攻毒,尽管部分动物出现短暂体重下降但大部分恢复,显示出LAIV在抗致死性感染方面优于灭活疫苗。 Live-attenuated vaccination limits viral replication in the nasal mucosa(减毒活疫苗接种限制鼻黏膜中的病毒复制):通过空斑试验检测鼻拭子样本,研究人员发现由于攻毒剂量较低(100 PFU),第1天未检测到病毒;第3天和第5天,两组疫苗接种组的病毒滴度均显著低于未接种组;攻毒后第7天,所有存活的灭活疫苗免疫雪貂中仍可检测到传染性病毒,而6只LAIV免疫雪貂中有4只未检测到病毒,且LAIV组病毒滴度显著低于灭活疫苗组,表明LAIV对鼻黏膜病毒复制的控制更为有效。 Inactivated vaccine and live attenuated vaccine reduce viral replication in organs(灭活疫苗和减毒活疫苗降低器官中的病毒复制):于攻毒后第3天采集每组4只雪貂的嗅球、脑、鼻甲、肺和气管组织进行病毒滴定,结果显示未接种组所有动物全部检测器官均检出病毒,两种疫苗均降低大多数器官的病毒滴度,但灭活疫苗组鼻甲的病毒滴度降低幅度有限;组织病理学检查显示未接种组肺部呈现肺泡炎,伴中性粒细胞和巨噬细胞浸润及浆液性渗出,严重者可见肺泡壁坏死,且坏死区域与流感病毒NP抗原检测阳性区域一致;灭活疫苗组病变严重程度个体差异较大;LAIV组总体肺泡病变更轻,病毒抗原检测多为阴性,提示LAIV对上呼吸道的病毒复制控制优于灭活疫苗。 Live attenuated vaccine induces a stronger cellular immune response than inactivated vaccine(减毒活疫苗诱导强于灭活疫苗的细胞免疫反应):研究人员未发现针对hu-TX37-H5N1的可检测中和抗体(血清及鼻洗液均为阴性);针对季节性疫苗株H1、H3及乙型HA的结合抗体滴度灭活疫苗组更高;针对H5N1的N1 NA和NP的交叉结合抗体也呈类似趋势;LAIV组血清可轻微但显著抑制N1蛋白活性,而灭活疫苗组无此活性;ELISpot检测显示LAIV诱导的针对H5N1 NP的T细胞反应(IFN-γ分泌)显著强于灭活疫苗。因此,保护性免疫可能与细胞免疫及可能的黏膜免疫相关,而非中和抗体。 研究人员在讨论中指出,两种疫苗均诱导针对疫苗株的免疫应答并降低病毒复制,但临床结局差异显著;保护差异无法用血清抗体解释,因灭活疫苗诱导了更高的HI滴度和结合抗体,而两组均未诱导针对hu-TX37-H5N1的中和抗体;LAIV的微弱NAI活性不足以单独解释其保护优势;LAIV诱导了更强的T细胞反应,识别NP等保守蛋白的T细胞可能交叉反应并与疾病缓解相关。研究亦存在局限:流感-na?ve雪貂两次接种不能完全模拟人类既有免疫;缺乏雪貂特异性试剂,无法充分评估呼吸道局部分泌型免疫应答;部分灭活疫苗组动物在攻毒后晚期死亡,死亡原因不明。 研究结论指出,季节性减毒活流感疫苗接种可为流感-na?ve雪貂提供针对致死性hu-TX37-H5N1感染的实质性保护,而灭活疫苗虽可降低病毒复制并延缓疾病进展,但无法预防死亡;保护性免疫可能依赖于血清抗体之外的细胞免疫及潜在黏膜免疫应答,为应对奶牛源H5N1病毒的交叉保护策略提供了实验依据。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 source_language_evidence.location_and_population: Live attenuated vaccination protects ferrets from lethal hu-TX37-H5N1 infection(减毒活疫苗接种保护雪貂抵抗致死性hu-TX37-H5N1感染):以100 PFU的hu-TX37-H5N1进行鼻内攻毒后,未接种组11只雪貂全部出现进行性体重下降及/或体温降低,并在8天内死亡或达到人道处死标准;接种灭活疫苗的雪貂同样发生严重疾病,全部在12天内死亡或被人道处死,但存活时间较未接种组明显延迟,表明灭活疫苗仅提供部分保护;而接种LAIV的6只雪貂中有5只存活攻毒,尽管部分动物出现短暂体重下降但大部分恢复,显示出LAIV在抗致死性感染方面优于灭活疫苗。
source_language_evidence.event: 季节性流感疫苗对奶牛源人源H5N1流感病毒(A/Texas/37/2024)的交叉保护效应:减毒活疫苗通过细胞免疫提供抗致死性感染的保护 - 生物通。
source_language_evidence.scale_impact_and_risk: Live-attenuated vaccination limits viral replication in the nasal mucosa(减毒活疫苗接种限制鼻黏膜中的病毒复制):通过空斑试验检测鼻拭子样本,研究人员发现由于攻毒剂量较低(100 PFU),第1天未检测到病毒;第3天和第5天,两组疫苗接种组的病毒滴度均显著低于未接种组;攻毒后第7天,所有存活的灭活疫苗免疫雪貂中仍可检测到传染性病毒,而6只LAIV免疫雪貂中有4只未检测到病毒,且LAIV组病毒滴度显著低于灭活疫苗组,表明LAIV对鼻黏膜病毒复制的控制更为有效。
source_language_evidence.response_status_and_uncertainty: Live attenuated vaccine induces a stronger cellular immune response than inactivated vaccine(减毒活疫苗诱导强于灭活疫苗的细胞免疫反应):研究人员未发现针对hu-TX37-H5N1的可检测中和抗体(血清及鼻洗液均为阴性);针对季节性疫苗株H1、H3及乙型HA的结合抗体滴度灭活疫苗组更高;针对H5N1的N1 NA和NP的交叉结合抗体也呈类似趋势;LAIV组血清可轻微但显著抑制N1蛋白活性,而灭活疫苗组无此活性;ELISpot检测显示LAIV诱导的针对H5N1 NP的T细胞反应(IFN-γ分泌)显著强于灭活疫苗。因此,保护性免疫可能与细胞免疫及可能的黏膜免疫相关,而非中和抗体。

To learn more, view the following link: Privacy Policy Manage Preferences Storage Preferences Log In Subscribe News Government Elections Wildfires Sports Business Opinion Submit An Opinion Lifestyle Events Contests Newsletters Classifieds Public Notices Bid Notices Place An Ad Special Sections Amazing Kids Nomination Community Heroes Nomination Salute to Veterans Nomination Amazing Educators Nomination Home Weather Newsletters Contact Us About Us Special Sections Amazing Kids Nomination Community Heroes Nomination Salute to Veterans Nomination Amazing Educators Nomination Business News Government Elections Wildfires Opinion Submit An Opinion Sports Events Contests Public Notices Bid Notices Classifieds Public Notices Bid Notices Place An Ad Puzzles & Games Bird flu cases continue in Oregon, Washington Published 1:37 pm Tuesday, November 24, 2026 By Kyle Odegard A worker in biosecurity gear tends to a flock. Highly pathogenic avian influenza tends to reemerge in the fall as migrating waterfowl, which carry the virus, return to regions. (USDA/Contributed) Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... California farm loses 89,000 birds in mid-November case Cases of highly pathogenic avian influenza continued to occur in non-commercial backyard flocks in Oregon and Washington in mid-November, according to USDA data. Oregon had bird flu cases Nov. 19 in Marion County and on Nov. 20 in Clatsop County. In each instance, 40 birds were euthanized. Washington had cases in Pierce County on Nov. 17, which killed 60 birds, and on Nov. 20, when 10 birds were affected. The most significant instance of HPAI in the West in mid-November came Nov. 18 from Fresno County, Calif., where 88,900 birds in a commercial broiler breeder operation were killed. In late October and early November, however, California and each state in the Pacific Northwest had major commercial cases. The disease began to reemerge at that time because wild waterfowl spread the virus as they migrate. An Oct. 28 case affected 1.3 million birds at a commercial egg layer in Stanislaus County, Calif. On Nov. 4, HPAI killed 94,200 birds at a commercial egg layer facility in Clackamas County, Oregon. Also on Nov. 4, a Pierce County, Wash., commercial table egg operation lost 39,600 birds due to the disease. On Nov. 5, HPAI killed 7,000 birds at a commercial game bird farm in Gooding County, Idaho, according to USDA data. HPAI also hitting dairy herds Bird flu also is spreading in dairy herds. Oregon reported its first human case of HPAI this year on Nov. 19, which was connected to a recent case at a Morrow County dairy farm. On Nov. 1, a Yakima County, Wash., resident exposed to infected cattle died from bird flu. On Nov. 23, USDA confirmed bird flu in dairy cattle in Washington’s Grant County. Washington has now had 44 dairy herds stricken by avian influenza since the first case was confirmed Oct. 8. The Morrow County outbreak is Oregon’s only case of HPAI in dairy herds in the past 30 days, as of Nov. 24. HPAI has been detected in 17 cases in dairy herds in Washington during the past month. However, there have been more than 40 such instances in Washington since early October. Idaho has had two detections of HPAI in dairy herds in the past month, while California has had none. first case in Grant County Indonesia 24.11.2026 662 Authorities confirmed the first detection of avian influenza in dairy cattle in Grant County on November 23, 2026, making it the third affected county in Washington. The farm was quarantined; health authorities reiterated that commercially available pasteurized milk and dairy products are safe. The Washington State Department of Agriculture (WSDA) and the Grant Health District announced the detection, the first confirmed in the state since November 5. Washington recorded its first case on October 8, 2026, and previous outbreaks had been confined to Yakima and Benton counties. With 44 herds affected since October, the state is tied with Texas for fourth place nationally in detections of highly pathogenic avian influenza in cattle, behind California, Idaho and Colorado. Genetic sequencing and epidemiological investigations link the infections to cattle movements between states and farms, rather than introductions from wild birds. According to an analysis by the United States Department of Agriculture's Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS), the H5N1 genotype B3.13 detected in all three counties matches the virus introduced into Washington through cattle from Idaho. It subsequently spread among cows on different dairy farms. Veterinarians are treating sick animals at the Grant County farm, which is subject to strict biosecurity protocols. WSDA continues monthly bulk-tank milk testing and facility inspections statewide, alongside weekly surveillance in affected communities. State veterinarians urge prompt reporting of symptoms such as thicker milk ranging from yellowish to brown, sharp declines in milk production and feed intake, fever, respiratory problems, changes in manure and reduced rumination. Recommendations for producers include limiting movements of lactating cows between farms, isolating newly arrived animals for 30 days and avoiding sharing vehicles or equipment. They also advise separating cows suspected of infection, keeping abnormal milk out of bulk tanks and restricting cattle access to open water frequented by wild waterfowl. WSDA and the Grant Health District said pasteurization effectively inactivates H5N1 and that they do not anticipate milk shortages. Because infected cows shed the virus primarily through raw milk, health authorities advise consumers and pet owners to avoid unpasteurized dairy products. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Washington State Department of Health consider the risk to the general public low; no person-to-person transmission has been identified in the United States. Dairy workers face a higher risk of exposure and are advised to wear gloves, masks, eye protection and fluid-resistant coveralls. Washington has recorded three human cases among workers at Yakima dairy farms in 2026, including one death involving a person with underlying medical conditions. Over the past 30 days, the United States Department of Agriculture has confirmed infections in 26 dairy herds across seven states, including one case in neighboring Oregon. Since March 2024, the cumulative national total has reached 1,236 affected herds across 26 states.
