Why did H5N1 spread from Idaho to Washington dairies? topics: H5N1 Avian influenza Dairy cattle Quarantine Biosecurity Raw milk Pasteurization Washington GRANT COUNTY, Wash. — Highly pathogenic avian influenza has been confirmed in a Grant County dairy herd, prompting a quarantine and renewed calls for strict biosecurity as state and federal officials investigate how the virus is spreading between farms. The Washington State Department of Agriculture said on Nov. 23 that it identified highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) H5N1 in the herd. SEE ALSO | L&I inspects two Central Washington dairies after worker dies from bird flu The virus was detected by the Washington Animal Disease Diagnostic Laboratory through routine surveillance, and the finding was confirmed by the USDA National Veterinary Services Laboratories. USDA genetic sequencing analysis indicates the H5N1 strain currently circulating in Washington dairy herds is consistent with a virus introduced from Idaho through cattle movement. Powered By 10 Sec Seattleites turn to to-go Thanksgiving feasts, easing prep while boosting local economy Next Stay Investigations indicate the virus has spread from cow to cow between dairy herds. While wild birds can carry and spread HPAI, they are not believed to be the source of transmission between Washington dairy herds, WSDA said. The affected dairy herd is under quarantine and has employed strict biosecurity measures, according to WSDA. Veterinarians are working to treat sick cows. WSDA said pasteurized milk products remain safe for consumers and milk supply shortages are not expected. Pasteurization inactivates viruses and bacteria in milk, including HPAI virus, and consumers are urged to look for “pasteurized” or “ultra-pasteurized” on labels. WSDA warned that infected cows can shed the virus in their milk, making raw milk, cheese, and other raw unpasteurized dairy products unsafe for consumption. Health officials told consumers to avoid raw milk and raw dairy products, particularly those from infected or untested farms, because they may contain harmful viruses and bacteria. SEE ALSO | How concerned should you be about recent bird flu cases in Washington state? WSDA also advised people not to allow pets or other animals to consume raw milk or other dairy products, or raw foods such as raw meat or dead birds. WSDA urged dairy farmers statewide to report clinical signs of illness to their veterinarian, including changes in milk appearance (thicker, often yellowish to brown), decreased milk production, decline in feed intake, fever, respiratory symptoms, changes in manure, and a steep drop in rumination and rumen motility. The agency said affected animals should be isolated and farmers should contact their veterinarian and WSDA at 360-902-1878 or ahealth@agr.wa.gov. Most cattle affected by HPAI recover with supportive care, WSDA said, with full herd recovery typically taking four to six weeks. “I know another detection is discouraging, especially for the dairy farmers who have worked so hard to protect their workers and their herds. But I want to recognize what this community has accomplished. Dairy farmers across Eastern Washington have worked together, shared what they’ve learned and supported one another through an incredibly challenging time. The fact that we’ve been able to limit the virus’s spread across the region is a significant accomplishment and speaks to the dedication of our farmers, veterinarians and farmworkers,” said Washington State Veterinarian Amber Itle, VMD, MS. “I encourage everyone to keep going, stay the course and continue looking out for one another. The work you’re doing matters, and it is making a difference.” WSDA said HPAI can spread between dairy cattle through infected animals and contaminated milk, equipment, vehicles, clothing, footwear and other materials or people that move between farms. Wild birds can also carry HPAI, but they are considered a rare source of introduction and spread to dairy herds. Poultry are also highly susceptible to HPAI transmitted by any other affected species, and other states have reported infections in commercial and backyard poultry flocks near dairy farms affected by H5N1. Poultry owners, including those with backyard flocks, are urged to remain vigilant for signs of illness and practice strong biosecurity. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention and the Washington State Department of Health currently consider the risk to the public from avian influenza to be low, WSDA said. Advertisement Updated: 5:29 PM EST Nov 22, 2026 Editorial Standards i Allen Cone Assignment Editor Okeechobee egg farm tests positive for bird flu, will cull nearly 1.8M chickens Cal-Maine Foods halts production, state establishes quarantine zone Updated: 5:29 PM EST Nov 22, 2026 Editorial Standards i Allen Cone Assignment Editor OKEECHOBEE, Fla. — The largest egg company in the United States reported that its operation in Okeechobee County tested positive for highly pathogenic avian influenza, which will result in the ultimate depopulation of approximately 1.4 million laying hens and 360,000 pullets. Production has ceased at the plant, which follows the protocols prescribed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture on bird flu. The closure represents 2.7% of flock of the company, which is headquartered in Ridgeland, Mississippi. Advertisement "Cal-Maine Foods continues to work closely with federal, state and local government officials and focused industry groups to mitigate the risk of future outbreaks and effectively manage the response," the company said in a statement. The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services established a quarantine area that includes Okeechobee and stretches into St. Lucie County on Thursday. "Avian influenza is a serious disease concern for the poultry industry and animal health officials," the state agency said. "Influenza virus strains vary considerably in severity, and their pathogenicity, or ability to kill poultry, is labeled as either highly pathogenic with large mortality, or low pathogenic with little or no mortality." Florida Department of Agriculture Bird flu quarantine area. The agency regularly monitors domestic poultry for evidence of avian influenza viruses. Samples are regularly collected from backyard flocks, show birds, commercial poultry and live bird markets. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention c onsiders the risk to the general public to be low but the agency "is watching the situation carefully and working with states to monitor people with animal exposures." The CDC has reported 75 human cases of H5 bird flu and three deaths in the U.S. since February 2024: 45 involving dairy cattle, 24 poultry farms and three other animals. There are more than 378.5 million egg-laying chickens in the United States. In 2023, more than 9.4 billion broiler chickens and 218 million turkeys were processed in the United States. With measles surging, the US is likely to lose 'elimination' status. The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services established a quarantine zone covering Okeechobee and parts of St. Lucie County. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) stated that the risk to the general public is low, though they monitor individuals with animal exposures. Since February 2024, the CDC has reported 75 human cases and three deaths linked to H5 bird flu in the U.S. The company emphasized collaboration with federal, state, and local authorities to mitigate future outbreaks and manage the response effectively.

Bird flu confirmed in commercial poultry flock in Polk County Close By Samantha Nitz Published: Nov. 24, 2026 at 4:12 PM UTC Share Add Us On GoogleAdd as a preferred source on Google MADISON, Wis. (WEAU) - The Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection is announcing a confirmed case of highly pathogenic avian influenza in a commercial poultry flock in Polk County. According to a press release from the Wisconsin Department of Agriculture, Trade and Consumer Protection, DATCP and the U.S. Department of Agriculture animal health officials are working together in a joint incident response. The press release goes on to say the affected premises has been quarantined to restrict movement of poultry and poultry products, birds on the property have been depopulated to prevent the spread of the disease, and birds from the flock will not enter the food system. Additional information regarding highly pathogenic avian influenza in poultry is available HERE: DATCP Home Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza in Poultry. supplementary_news.title: Novel Avian Influenza Reassortant Virus Discovered in Chinese Poultry Outbreak
supplementary_news.excerpt: Researchers in China characterized a novel H6N2 avian influenza reassortant virus that combines a waterfowl-origin hemagglutinin gene with the internal cassette of poultry-adapted H9N2 viruses.

supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Friday, November 27, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Novel Avian Influenza Reassortant Virus Discovered in Chinese Poultry Outbreak by November 23, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 7 mins read 0 Novel Avian Influenza Reassortant Virus Discovered in Chinese Poultry Outbreak Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Veterinary researchers investigating an acute respiratory disease outbreak in commercial poultry in central China have identified and characterized a novel reassortant avian influenza virus designated A/chicken/Henan/NL04/2025, or NL04. The natural reassortant belongs to the low-pathogenic H6N2 subtype but carries an unusual genetic composition that combines external and internal gene segments from divergent avian influenza lineages. The outbreak occurred in December 2025 within a fifty-four-week-old commercial layer flock located in Shangqiu, Henan Province, causing severe respiratory symptoms and a fifteen percent cumulative mortality rate. Affected birds exhibited severe clinical signs including elevated body temperature, profound lethargy, reduced feed intake, neck extension during respiration, and acute death within three to four days of onset. Postmortem examinations of affected field birds showed severe bronchial obstruction caused by long white exudative plugs occluding the airways, which investigators identified as the primary cause of suffocation and death. Additional necropsy findings in the field flock revealed signs of yolk sac peritonitis, presenting a lesion severity substantially greater than that typically documented during standard low-pathogenic avian influenza infections. Whole-genome sequencing of the isolated NL04 strain revealed an intricate reassortment profile that integrates segments from two major circulating avian influenza lineages. The hemagglutinin gene was traced to a waterfowl-origin H6 lineage showing 96.59 percent nucleotide identity to known sequences and clustering within Eurasian group I, also designated the ST339-like lineage. In contrast, the neuraminidase gene derived from an H9N2 poultry lineage, exhibiting 99.37 percent nucleotide homology with contemporary circulating H9N2 isolates and falling within the Eurasian Y280-like lineage. Crucially, all six internal gene segments—PB2, PB1, PA, NP, M, and NS—were inherited from the chicken-adapted H9N2 G57 genotype, exhibiting high nucleotide identities between 96.38 percent and 99.12 percent. While initial sequence alignment identified top basic local alignment matches for the PB2 and M genes in H3N3 and H3N8 isolates, phylogenetic analyses demonstrated that those matching segments were themselves derived from circulating H9N2 G57 viruses. This genomic constellation demonstrates that NL04 did not acquire its internal segments through piecemeal genetic drift, but rather inherited an intact ribonucleoprotein cassette and structural core that is widely established in terrestrial poultry. Analysis of molecular virulence markers in the primary sequences revealed critical structural attributes governing host range, drug susceptibility, and baseline pathogenicity. The hemagglutinin cleavage site of the NL04 isolate possessed the sequence PQIETR↓G, lacking the consecutive basic amino acids that characterize highly pathogenic avian influenza viruses and thereby confirming its classification as a low-pathogenic strain. The canonical mammalian receptor-binding mutations Q226L and G228S were absent in the hemagglutinin protein, with residues Q226 and G228 fully preserved. However, analysis of the neuraminidase protein identified a deletion within the stalk region spanning residues 62 to 64, a structural change that has previously been linked to elevated virulence in mammalian hosts, alongside a K368N substitution associated with immune escape and antigenic drift. Within the matrix 2 protein, the isolate harbored the S31N substitution, which confers pharmacological resistance to the adamantane class of antiviral drugs, specifically amantadine. The six internal gene products contained numerous non-canonical substitutions previously documented to enhance polymerase activity and replication kinetics in distinct genetic backgrounds. The PB2 protein carried the specific substitutions A588V, T598I, and A676T, all associated with heightened viral replication and polymerase efficiency in experimental models, while lacking the canonical mammalian adaptive markers A199S, I292V, and E627K. In the PB1 protein, residues 473V and I368V were present, mutations linked respectively to enhanced polymerase performance in mammalian cell systems and respiratory droplet transmissibility in ferrets. The polymerase acidic subunit contained K356R, associated with enhanced mammalian replication, alongside the avian-mammalian species marker S409N. Further markers were detected in the nucleoprotein, where L3S was identified, and in the matrix 1 protein, which exhibited the species signature T215A and the virulence-associated change N30D. Finally, the non-structural protein NS1 carried four recognized substitutions—P42S, E172K, N205S, and P212S—known to modify virulence and interferon antagonism in mammalian experimental hosts. To rigorously determine the intrinsic biological behavior of the isolate without the confounding environmental variables of intensive farming, researchers inoculated two-week-old specific-pathogen-free chickens via combined ocular and intranasal routes using an infectious dose of 10^6.0 EID50. In stark contrast to the devastating fifteen percent mortality recorded in the commercial Henan flock, all inoculated specific-pathogen-free chickens survived the full fourteen-day experimental monitoring period. The infected birds displayed no overt clinical abnormalities, remaining free of fever, depression, lethargy, or diarrheal illness, and their body weight gain showed no statistically significant difference when compared with uninfected phosphate-buffered saline control animals. Gross pathological evaluation performed at three days post-infection showed only subtle organ changes, including focal hemorrhagic spots within the Harderian gland, mild enlargement and petechial hemorrhages in the thymus, and slight bursal swelling with minor mucoid exudation, while respiratory organs such as the trachea and lungs showed no macroscopic lesions. Despite the lack of overt clinical illness and visible macroscopic pathology in experimental chickens, microscopic histopathological evaluation revealed extensive underlying tissue damage throughout the respiratory tract. Examination of hematoxylin and eosin-stained tracheal sections demonstrated severe ciliary shedding along the epithelial lining without overt hemorrhagic extravasation. In lung sections, alveolar atrophy was prominent and accompanied by substantial infiltration of inflammatory cells into interstitial spaces, while kidney tissues showed glomerular epithelial karyopyknosis with erythrocyte and leukocyte infiltration. Immunohistochemical staining confirmed viral replication in the respiratory epithelium, revealing abundant viral nucleoprotein antigen in lung alveolar epithelial cells. Semi-quantitative histopathological scoring confirmed that tissue lesions were most severe in the lungs and trachea, followed by the kidneys. Quantitative viral titration of tissues at three days post-infection established that viral replication peaked in the upper respiratory tract and associated ocular tissues, reaching 10^5.56 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in the nasal turbinates and 10^4.23 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in the Harderian gland, while trachea and bronchus titers both reached 10^1.82 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter, confirming strict respiratory tropism. The marked discrepancy between mild experimental laboratory infections in specific-pathogen-free chickens and the severe mortality observed in the commercial Henan flock highlights the profound influence of secondary production factors. In industrial poultry operations, high-density stocking, environmental ammonia accumulation, ventilation stress, and concurrent microbial exposures create an environment highly permissive to exacerbated clinical disease. Primary viral replication by low-pathogenic strains such as NL04 damages the respiratory ciliated epithelium and compromises mucociliary clearance, rendering birds highly vulnerable to secondary opportunistic bacterial invaders such as Escherichia coli and Mycoplasma species. These secondary pathogens frequently induce severe exudative fibrinous airsacculitis and bronchial occlusion, explaining the fatal plugs observed in the commercial outbreak. The experimental findings emphasize that specific-pathogen-free animal trials alone cannot predict the true veterinary and economic impact of emerging avian influenza variants in real-world commercial poultry operations. To evaluate potential mammalian spillover risk, the research team intranasally challenged six-week-old female BALB/c mice with 10^6.00 EID50 of the purified NL04 virus. Over the fourteen-day evaluation period, all infected mice survived without displaying detectable respiratory distress, ruffled fur, or statistically significant weight loss relative to sham-inoculated controls. Organ titration at three days post-infection demonstrated limited replication, with viral titers confined predominantly to the upper respiratory tract at 10^3.25 EID50 per 0.1 milliliter in nasal turbinates, accompanied by minimal levels of 10^1.56 in lung tissue and 10^1.18 in kidney tissue. Brain samples showed no viral replication, and histological sections revealed only mild alveolar inflammatory infiltration without structural necrosis. In vitro replication kinetics comparing Madin-Darby canine kidney cells and primary chick embryo fibroblasts revealed rapid viral propagation in both cell types, though avian fibroblasts supported significantly higher viral yields during early replication phases between 12 and 48 hours post-infection. These mammalian studies demonstrate that despite bearing several molecular adaptation markers, NL04 possesses limited mammalian replication competence and low intrinsic pathogenicity in mice. Global epidemiological analysis of 5,029 historical H6Ny avian influenza isolates cataloged from 1963 to 2025 provided broader context on subtype evolution, ecological reservoirs, and interspecies transmission events. Annual isolation numbers remained low through the late 1990s before expanding sharply into an ongoing elevated circulation plateau that peaked in 2014 with approximately 440 recorded isolates. Avian species constituted the predominant ecological niche, representing 91.7 percent of the total dataset, whereas environmental samples accounted for 6.4 percent, and mammalian and human isolations remained exceptionally scarce at four and two cases respectively. Among the nine recognized neuraminidase pairings, H6N2 and H6N6 emerged as the dominant subtypes globally, accounting for 30.98 percent and 28.08 percent of all isolates, followed by H6N1 at 17.24 percent. While wild aquatic waterfowl constitute the natural ancestral reservoir, the surveillance dataset documented 145 separate spillover events of H6N2 into domestic chickens, demonstrating that terrestrial poultry now represent an established secondary niche that facilitates frequent encounters and reassortment with endemic poultry viruses. Given the commercial risks posed by circulating reassortants, the researchers formulated and tested a whole-inactivated oil-emulsion vaccine candidate derived from the homologous NL04 strain. Purified allantoic virus was inactivated using 0.1 percent beta-propiolactone for 24 hours at four degrees Celsius, followed by beta-propiolactone hydrolysis at thirty-seven degrees Celsius and high-speed emulsification with Montanide ISA 78 VG adjuvant. Three-week-old specific-pathogen-free chickens received a single intramuscular injection of 0.3 milliliters of the prepared vaccine formulation, with control animals receiving adjuvant-emulsified saline. Serum hemagglutination inhibition titers monitored weekly reached a mean of 13.25 log2 by five weeks post-immunization, confirming the induction of a potent humoral immune response. Following homologous live virus challenge at five weeks, vaccinated birds exhibited a substantially shortened and restricted shedding profile, shedding virus exclusively through the oral route and clearing infection within four days, whereas unvaccinated control birds shed virus predominantly through the oral route across the first week post-challenge. Neutralization assays conducted in embryonated chicken eggs further demonstrated that post-vaccination antisera effectively neutralized the homologous NL04 virus and exhibited cross-protective neutralizing activity against a heterologous H6N1 isolate collected from poultry in December 2025. In both cases, incubation of serum-virus mixtures abolished detectable hemagglutinating activity in harvested allantoic fluid, confirming that vaccine-induced antibodies recognize shared antigenic epitopes across distinct H6 lineages. The investigators identified key study limitations, including the lack of quantitative in vitro receptor-binding assays, the absence of aerosol droplet transmission experiments, the reliance on a single field isolate, and the need for vaccine efficacy validation under commercial field conditions with secondary pathogens. Nonetheless, the investigation underscores that the continuous genetic exchange between waterfowl-origin surface glycoproteins and the robust H9N2 G57 internal ribonucleoprotein machinery produces resilient reassortants capable of threatening commercial poultry health, highlighting the urgent need for sustained poultry genomic surveillance. Home Prayer Updates Devotional Donate Close Menu Search for: Home Prayer Updates Devotional Donate Close Menu Home › Prayer Updates › USDA Addresses H5N1 Outbreak in Dairy Herds USDA Addresses H5N1 Outbreak in Dairy Herds Prayer Updates Posted on November 23, 2026 • Updated November 19, 2026 —by The Presidential Prayer Team639 The avian flu has been confirmed in herds in Indiana and Washington. The U.S. Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) National Veterinary Services Laboratories (NVSL) has recently confirmed the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), aka bird flu, in certain herds in Washington state and Indiana. Officials noted that “the original spillover event... was detected in the Texas Panhandle in late 2023.” The USDA stated, “This detection does not pose a risk to consumer health or affect the safety of the commercial milk supply. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration is confident that pasteurization is effective at inactivating HPAI virus, and that the commercial, pasteurized milk supply is safe.” The agency added, “Dairies are required to send only milk from healthy animals into processing for human consumption; milk from impacted animals is being diverted from the commercial milk tank or destroyed so that it does not enter the human food supply.” The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) continues to consider the risk to the public to be low. The agency said that H5 is widespread in wild birds worldwide. As the Lord Leads, Pray with Us... For Secretary Rollins as she oversees the USDA and its evaluation of agricultural animal health. For Administrator Kelly Moore as she heads APHIS and seeks to ensure the health of dairy cows. For farmers and ranchers as they work to eliminate and mitigate the spread of influenza among their herds. Health Quarantine in place north of Okeechobee to stop spread of bird flu; State must sign off movement WGCU | By Combined dispatches Published November 22, 2026 at 4:19 PM EST Facebook LinkedIn Email Print Sad chickens in cage to sell or eat. Cage farming. Concept of animal protection The Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) established a quarantine area north of Okeechobee Nov. 19 to prevent the spread of highly pathogenic avian influenza, commonly known as bird flu. Okeechobee County is urging poultry owners to check the state’s quarantine map before moving birds or poultry products. Under the state quarantine, all poultry and poultry products require FDACS permission to move within, into or out of the designated area. Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services Avian influenza quarantine area To request permission, email the FDACS Division of Animal Industry at RAD@FDACS.gov. For questions about the quarantine, call 850-410-0900. The official quarantine map and state notice are available at FDACS.gov/ai. Support for WGCU Provided By: Dr. Ben Anderson, an assistant professor in the University of Florida’s Department of Environmental and Global Health, said H5N1 primarily affects wild migratory birds and can cause serious illness and economic losses in domestic poultry. “Although outbreaks in poultry can have substantial impacts on affected farms and poultry owners, the risk to the general public remains low,” Anderson said. Residents should avoid handling sick or dead birds. Backyard flock owners and commercial poultry producers should follow recommended biosecurity practices, including keeping their flocks separate from wild birds. Eggs and poultry products remain safe to eat when properly handled and thoroughly cooked. How to report sick or dead birds: • Wild birds. Contact the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission (FWC) Wildlife Alert Hotline at 888-404-FWCC (3922) or submit a report at MyFWC.com/Bird. • Domestic poultry. Report unusual illness or unexplained deaths to FDACS at 850-410-0900 during business hours, 800-342-5869 after hours, or RAD@FDACS.gov. Additional resources • FDACS quarantine map and avian influenza information https://www.fdacs.gov/ai • FWC avian influenza information https://myfwc.com/research/wildlife/health/avian/influenza/ • USDA APHIS avian disease information https://www.aphis.usda.gov/livestock-poultry-disease/avian • UF/IFAS bird flu resources https://piecenter.com/resources/birdflu/ Printed copies of this information are available at the UF/IFAS Extension Okeechobee County office, located at 458 U.S. Highway 98 North. If you have questions or concerns, call the Extension office at 863-763-6469. WGCU is your trusted source for news and information in Southwest Florida. We are a nonprofit public service, and your support is more critical than ever. Keep public media strong and donate now. Thank you. 美国华盛顿州报告3例人感染H5N1禽流感病例 其中1人死亡 ©粮农组织/哈希姆·阿齐兹 奶牛场 Weibo Twitter 打印 电子邮件 美国华盛顿州报告3例人感染H5N1禽流感病例 其中1人死亡 2026年11月24日 健康及卫生 世界卫生组织周二发布疫情通报称,美国华盛顿州报告3例经实验室确诊的甲型H5N1禽流感病毒人类感染病例,其中包括1例死亡病例。这是全球首例因接触受感染奶牛或相关受污染环境而导致的死亡病例。 3名患者均为18岁以上成年人,在华盛顿州亚基马县奶牛场工作。该地区近期在奶牛中检测到高致病性甲型H5N1禽流感病毒。世卫组织表示,目前尚无证据表明存在人际传播。根据现有信息,世卫组织评估认为,该病毒对普通人群构成的风险较低,对因职业原因接触病毒的人员构成的风险处于低至中等水平。 3例感染病例中1人死亡 世卫组织于10月16日接到美国通报,华盛顿州出现1例经实验室确诊的甲型H5流感病毒人类感染病例;11月4日又接到通报,该州新增2例确诊病例,其中1例死亡。 首例患者于10月5日出现眼部刺激、流涕、肌肉酸痛和头痛等症状,未住院,接受了抗流感病毒药物奥司他韦(达菲)治疗。 第二例患者患有基础疾病,出现呼吸道症状后因病情严重住院,并于11月1日死亡。 第三例患者出现结膜炎症状,但无需住院治疗。 对3例病例中病毒的基因测序证实,感染病毒均属于甲型H5N1流感病毒亚型。病毒序列与华盛顿州奶牛中检测到的病毒高度相似。 美国农业部11月4日报告称,对华盛顿州首批两处受影响奶牛群中的病毒进行全基因组测序后,确定其基因型为B3.13。基因分析显示,病毒可能通过牛只调运从爱达荷州传入。 截至2026年11月20日,自2024年以来,美国共报告75例甲型H5流感病毒感染病例,其中包括此次通报的3例。 尚无证据表明存在人际传播 世卫组织指出,动物流感病毒通常在动物群体中传播,但部分病毒具有感染人类的潜力。人类感染主要通过直接接触受感染动物或接触受污染环境发生。 人类感染禽流感病毒可能引起从轻微结膜炎和上呼吸道症状到严重、危及生命的疾病。 世卫组织表示,这3例病例均与在亚基马县职业性接触奶牛有关,病毒测序结果与当地奶牛中检测到的病毒高度相似,支持动物传人传播的判断。 目前,美国尚未发现甲型H5流感病毒的人际传播。全球范围内虽然曾有少量有限人际传播事件报告,但迄今尚未发现持续性人际传播。 针对受感染动物或受污染环境的接触人员,以及确诊病例的密切接触者,公共卫生调查、监测和追踪工作仍在进行。 加强监测和个人防护 美国联邦、州和地方公共卫生部门已采取应对措施,包括调查确诊病例及其动物接触史、监测密切接触者和接触过受感染动物的人员,并对出现症状者开展流感检测。 有关部门还向可能接触病毒的工作人员提供症状识别、检测和降低暴露风险的信息,并倡导和提供适当的个人防护装备。 美国疾病控制与预防中心建议,对接触过疑似或确诊感染禽流感病毒的禽类或其他动物的人员,在最后一次接触后最长10天内监测相关症状。接触后出现呼吸道症状或结膜炎的人员应接受流感检测。 世卫组织也建议识别和监测高危人群,加强对职业暴露人员的监测,并采取措施减少接触受感染动物和受污染环境。 避免接触受感染动物和饮用生奶 世卫组织建议公众避免在没有防护的情况下接触患病或死亡的动物,以及可能被受感染动物污染的环境。因工作原因接触可能受感染动物或受污染环境的人员,应使用适当的个人防护装备,并遵循感染预防和职业健康措施。 鉴于已在奶牛中检测到甲型H5N1流感病毒,世卫组织建议避免饮用生奶或未经巴氏杀菌的牛奶及生乳制品。巴氏杀菌牛奶及乳制品可以安全食用。食品加工过程中,应妥善烹饪和处理鸡蛋、禽肉及其他禽类产品。 世卫组织指出,目前尚无可立即用于人类的甲型H5流感疫苗。针对多个甲型H5病毒分支,已经选定用于大流行防备的候选疫苗病毒株。现有季节性流感疫苗不太可能对甲型H5禽流感病毒提供保护。 世卫组织强调,应继续开展全球监测,及时共享病毒和基因序列数据,加强人类、动物和环境卫生部门之间的协作。 世卫组织不建议针对这一事件在入境口岸实施特殊筛查,目前也不建议采取任何旅行或贸易限制。 禽流感 世界卫生组织 Weibo Twitter 打印 电子邮件 Back to top

the constrained evolution of H7N9 PB2 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月26日 来源:Poultry Science 4.5 编辑推荐: H7N9流感病毒是一种具有重大公共卫生意义的禽源性人畜共患病原体。PB2基因是H7N9流感病毒哺乳动物适应的关键决定因子,然而其适应性进化究竟是通过广泛的序列多样化推进,还是通过对有限数量允许位点的反复修饰实现,目前仍不明确。研究人员分析了来自中国的1555条 立即索取尼帕病毒研究试剂的详细技术资料>> 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Open access H7N9流感病毒是一种具有重大公共卫生意义的禽源性人畜共患病原体。PB2基因是H7N9流感病毒哺乳动物适应的关键决定因子,然而其适应性进化究竟是通过广泛的序列多样化推进,还是通过对有限数量允许位点的反复修饰实现,目前仍不明确。研究人员分析了来自中国的1555条PB2序列,综合运用密码子使用分析、选择压力推断、共变异网络重构和蛋白结构映射等方法。结果显示,PB2在全局层面受到强烈的蛋白功能约束,表现为弱密码子偏好、低密码子适应指数(CAI)以及广泛的纯化选择。尽管整体高度保守,适应性信号却集中分布于少数氨基酸残基:627位点在所有时间分组中均被反复检测到,591位点和701位点也在多个年份中出现。这些热点位点在选择模式上呈现时间异质性,并嵌入具有区域特征的位点关联网络中。结构映射显示,591、627和701位点在PB2功能相关区域内具有空间邻近性。置换检验表明,这些位点并未构成统计学上显著过度聚集的几何簇,但其空间邻近性支持其作为候选功能网络。总体而言,这些发现支持如下模型:PB2进化在全序列水平上受到约束,但通过一组有限的适应性热点位点反复优化,并表现出时间、地理和结构层面的组织特征,提示宿主适应可能沿受限的进化解空间推进,而非无约束的序列多样化。 H7N9流感病毒是近年来具有重要公共卫生意义的禽源性人畜共患流感病毒之一。自2013年在中国东部首次报告人感染病例以来,H7N9病毒在多个流行季中表现出复杂的宿主来源、地理扩散和基因重配特征,并与活禽暴露及活禽市场环境密切相关。PB2(聚合酶碱性蛋白2,polymerase basic protein 2)是流感病毒RNA依赖的RNA聚合酶复合体(RNA-dependent RNA polymerase complex)的重要组成部分,参与病毒基因组复制、转录起始和聚合酶活性调控。与HA(血凝素,hemagglutinin)和NA(神经氨酸酶,neuraminidase)等表面蛋白不同,PB2并不直接决定受体结合或抗原变异,但对不同宿主细胞中的复制效率、宿主范围和哺乳动物适应具有关键影响。既往研究多聚焦于PB2-627、PB2-701和PB2-591等单个宿主适应位点,或基于代表株、有限序列和单一流行阶段进行描述,较少从大规模自然序列出发,系统整合时间、地区、宿主背景、密码子使用、非同义选择压力、区域共进化网络和三维蛋白结构分布。因此,仅依靠系统发育树或经典突变频率统计,难以揭示H7N9 PB2在自然流行过程中是否具有时间重复性、地理协同性和结构模块性。基于这一问题,研究人员利用中国来源的人源和禽源H7N9全长PB2序列,构建整合谱系背景、密码子偏好、位点正选择、全基因选择压力、地理共变异网络和蛋白结构映射的多层分析框架,检验如下假设:在弱密码子偏好和保守编码约束背景下,PB2适应性进化由有限数量适应性热点的反复选择驱动。 ELISpot检测试剂盒新品上线中,立即索取技术资料>>领 取 在方法层面,研究人员以GISAID数据库中中国分离的人源和禽源H7N9全长PB2序列为研究对象,经开放阅读框完整性、模糊碱基比例、终止密码子和移码过滤后获得1555条序列;随后进行多序列比对和末端修剪,并基于最大似然法(maximum likelihood,ML)重建系统发育树以划分进化簇。进一步采用CodonW计算有效密码子数(effective number of codons,ENC)、密码子适应指数(codon adaptation index,CAI)、密码子偏好指数(codon bias index,CBI)、最优密码子使用频率(frequency of optimal codons,Fop)、第三位密码子GC含量(GC3s)和相对同义密码子使用度(relative synonymous codon usage,RSCU),并结合ENC-plot、PR2-bias和中性度分析评估突变压力与选择约束;利用Datamonkey和HyPhy进行MEME(mixed-effects model of evolution)位点正选择检测、BUSTED(branch-site unrestricted statistical test for episodic diversification)基因水平选择压力分析和BGM(Bayesian graphical models)位点共变异网络重构;最后将关键位点映射到PB2蛋白结构并进行置换检验。 研究结果显示,PB2整体处于强烈的功能约束之下。系统发育与流行病学特征映射表明,1555条PB2序列可划分为3个主要进化簇,人源与禽源序列在多个簇中交织分布,未形成完全独立的宿主单系群;长江三角洲、珠江三角洲及其他地区序列也分散于不同簇中,年度分布同样跨簇存在,说明PB2传播并非单一谱系线性替代,而是多谱系共存与扩散。密码子使用分析显示,PB2序列的GC3s主要集中在0.40至0.44,ENC主要集中在48至53,整体密码子偏好较弱;人源与禽源组的ENC中位数接近,地区间差异有限,而年份和进化簇之间差异更明显。CAI中位数约为0.149至0.153,CBI在各组均为负值,Fop约为0.343至0.357,说明PB2并未明显追求宿主最优密码子,而是维持一种次优但稳定的翻译水平。ENC-plot中多数点位低于仅由突变压力决定的理论曲线,PR2-bias显示第三位密码子整体偏向A和G,中性度分析中GC12与GC3s多呈负相关,表明PB2密码子组成并非中性随机,而受到自然选择、编码功能约束、RNA结构、宿主环境和谱系背景共同影响。 在时间选择压力方面,研究人员按2013、2014、2015、2017及其他年份分组进行MEME和BUSTED分析。MEME检测到各年份均存在阶段性正选择位点,但位点并非均匀分布于全长基因,而相对集中于PB2中部至C端区域;2017年检测到15个位点,2014年14个,2013年和2015年各12个,其他年份9个。627位点在全部时间组中均被检测到,是最稳定的跨年份正选择热点;109、591和701位点也在多个年份出现。BUSTED显示,2013年以纯化选择成分为主但ω3强度最高,提示早期可能由少数位点承受较强正选择;2014、2015、2017及其他年份中性或近中性成分升高,2017和其他年份正选择位点比例相对较高,提示后期可能存在更广泛但强度较低的位点微调。 在地理共进化方面,BGM网络显示PB2位点关联具有明显区域差异。长江三角洲网络复杂度中等,包含551-714、292-613、191-217、5-511、606-616、277-565和620-621等关联位点对,其中435、535和714连接较为突出;珠江三角洲网络更紧凑,582-584、513-619、341-385、467-566和451-475等位点对较显著,619位点在区域网络中连接作用突出;其他地区合并组网络最复杂,包含119-446、168-277、18-164、109-290、384-676、418-725、577-586、535-676、659-713和107-755等多组关联。该结果说明PB2共变关系不仅来自单个位点选择,也受到地区传播结构、遗传背景和位点间统计依赖关系影响;但BGM只能提示候选共进化关系,不能单独证明直接结构互作或功能上位性。 在结构映射方面,研究人员将591、627、701等核心时间重复正选择位点,589、619、714等辅助位点,以及435、535、464等区域共进化支持位点映射到7QTL结构。结果显示,591、627和701位于PB2 C端结构域表面附近,观察平均两两距离为23.48 ?,域内置换检验零分布均值为29.01 ± 8.08 ?,Z=-0.68,P=0.2527,说明三者并未形成统计学上显著过度紧密的几何簇,但具有空间邻近性,可解释为候选功能网络。589、619和714分布在核心位点周围,可能构成局部辅助层;435、535和464相对分散,体现区域共进化位点与核心正选择位点之间既有关联又保持相对独立的结构定位。 讨论部分指出,H7N9 PB2的进化不能简化为随机突变累积或单一位点驱动,而应理解为弱密码子偏好和强功能约束背景下,有限适应性热点的反复优化。627位点是跨年份最稳定的核心信号,591和701与其共同构成中部至C端适应性区域;589、619、714、759等位点在特定时间或区域中可能提供辅助调节,435、535、464等共变位点则可能反映区域遗传背景下的补偿或长程结构支持。该研究的重要意义在于,将分子监测思路从单一突变筛查推进到关键位点组合、谱系背景、时间阶段、地理网络和结构模块的联合评估,为禽源流感病毒跨宿主适应风险评估提供了多层证据框架。同时,研究人员也指出时间采样不均衡、其他年份和其他地区合并组存在混合效应、BGM结果缺乏实验验证、CAI/CBI/Fop依赖参考密码子集合等限制,后续仍需反向遗传学、聚合酶活性实验和分子动力学模拟进一步验证候选位点组合的功能效应。 原文结论部分可译为:总之,本研究揭示了中国H7N9流感病毒PB2片段的多层进化特征。PB2在系统发育上表现为多谱系共存,在密码子使用上呈弱但非中性的偏好,在选择压力上具有明显时间异质性,在不同地理区域中形成不同的统计共变网络,并且候选热点位点位于蛋白结构中功能相关区域。这些结果共同表明,H7N9 PB2的分子进化并非由随机漂变或单一突变简单驱动,而是受到全基因功能约束、局部正选择、区域相关协同替换和结构模块适应性共同塑造。总体而言,研究结果为如下模型提供支持:H7N9 PB2在全序列水平受到约束,但通过一组有限适应性热点反复优化,这些热点具有时间、地理和结构组织特征。这一模式提示,宿主适应可能沿受限的进化解空间推进,而非无约束的序列多样化;该框架可推动监测重点从单个突变转向重现热点的时空与结构背景。 打赏 展开全文 开通VIP 享海量文章 全站开放获取+解锁超过 200万篇新闻全文+每日更新 2000+篇,学术前沿动态全时追踪! supplementary_news.content: 臺北市 美國牛傳人H5N1禽流感死亡案例全球首見 藍雀新傳媒 藍雀新傳媒/magpieoffice 發布: 2026/11/25 12:19 (台灣時間) 資料更新: 2026/11/25 12:34 (台灣時間) 上圖說, ©糧農組織/哈希姆·阿齊茲 乳牛場 陳麗英整理編輯 (WHO)於2026年11月24日發布疫情通報,美國華盛頓州出現3例經實驗室確診的甲型H5N1禽流感病毒人類感染病例,其中1人不幸身亡。這是全球首例因接觸受感染乳牛或相關受污染環境而導致的死亡個案,引發國際公共衛生高度關注。 據通報指出,3名患者均為18歲以上成年人,且都在華盛頓州亞基馬縣(Yakima County)的乳牛場工作。首例患者於10月5日出現眼部刺激、流涕、肌肉酸痛與頭痛等症狀,經服用抗流感藥物奧司他韋(達菲)後未需住院;第二例患者本身患有潛在疾病,出現呼吸道症狀後因病情惡化住院,最終於11月1日不治;第三例患者則僅出現結膜炎,無須住院治療。 經基因定序確認,3名患者感染的病毒皆屬甲型H5N1亞型,基因序列與當地乳牛群檢測出的病毒高度相似。美國農業部指出,該病毒基因型為B3.13,研判可能透過牛隻調運自愛達荷州傳入。統計自2024年以來至2026年11月20日,美國已累計通報75例甲型H5流感人類感染病例。 針對疫情風險,世衛組織表示目前尚無證據顯示存在人際傳播,病毒對一般大眾的風險仍屬較低,但對職業暴露人員則為低至中等風險。目前美國聯邦與地方衛生部門已加強密切接觸者追蹤,並為農牧從業人員提供個人防護裝備與10天健康監測建議。 世衛組織呼籲民眾切勿在無防護下接觸生病或死亡動物,並避免飲用未經巴氏殺菌的生乳及生乳製品;經過巴氏殺菌的乳製品及徹底煮熟的禽蛋肉類則可安全食用。此外,現有季節性流感疫苗無法對H5禽流感提供保護,各國仍須持續強化跨部門疫情監測與資訊共享。(以下空白) 相關新聞 左右分流變路口交鋒 熱心駕駛助警還原真相 台灣好報 1 天前 Muse進入IG私訊,可整理收藏、規劃行程,台灣未列本輪名單 媒角抵加News 2 天前 台股狂飆逾 外資卻連賣!籌碼未穩防追高 00981T「債 7 股 3」成避風港 觀傳媒 2 天前 選前重砲轟擊 前議員孫金清點名鄉長候選人:恩將仇報! 觀傳媒 2 天前 輝達狂歡退潮 關稅變數再起!全球股市震盪加劇 00981T股債雙核兼顧收益與成長 觀傳媒 2 天前 百億股利活水到!台股震盪洗牌月配ETF兩樣情 00981T抗跌成防守焦點 觀傳媒 2 天前 台股修正潮凸顯資產分散價值 高股息近一個月跌兩成 「債券ETF」00945B逆勢上漲 觀傳媒 2 天前 跟著大戶躲股災「賣股轉債」! 三大法人月買逾4.8萬張 00945B大戶持股攀升 觀傳媒 2 天前 沈伯洋:11月28日後,我就是台北市政府的人、我是台北市長 品觀點 2 天前 AI時代怎麼選系?全臺攏學高中生營隊回饋看見職涯探索需求 商傳媒 2 天前

有关部门于2026年11月23日确认,格兰特县奶牛首次检出禽流感病毒,成为华盛顿州第三个受影响的县。涉事养殖场已被隔离;卫生部门重申,市售经巴氏杀菌的牛奶和乳制品可以安全食用。 华盛顿州农业部(WSDA)与格兰特卫生区宣布检出病毒,这是该州自11月5日以来首次确诊。华盛顿州于2026年10月8日报告首例病例,此前疫情集中在亚基马县和本顿县。自10月以来,该州已有44个奶牛群受到影响,牛群高致病性禽流感检出数量与得克萨斯州并列全美第四,仅次于加利福尼亚州、爱达荷州和科罗拉多州。 基因测序和流行病学调查表明,感染与跨州及养殖场之间的牛只运输有关,而非由野生鸟类传入。根据美国农业部动植物卫生检验局(APHIS)的分析,三个县检出的H5N1病毒B3.13基因型,与通过来自爱达荷州的牛只传入华盛顿州的病毒一致。随后,病毒在不同奶牛养殖场的牛只之间传播。 兽医正在治疗格兰特县涉事养殖场的患病动物,该养殖场已实施严格的生物安全措施。华盛顿州农业部继续每月对全州储奶罐中的牛奶及养殖设施进行检测,并每周对受影响地区及当地社区开展监测。州兽医呼吁及时报告以下症状:牛奶变稠、颜色呈淡黄色至棕色,产奶量和采食量大幅下降,发热、呼吸系统问题、粪便变化以及反刍减少。 对养殖户的建议包括:限制泌乳牛在养殖场之间转运,对新引进的动物隔离30天,并避免共用车辆或设备。此外,还建议将疑似感染的奶牛单独隔离,防止异常牛奶流入集中储奶罐,并限制牛只接触野生水禽经常活动的露天水域。 华盛顿州农业部与格兰特卫生区表示,巴氏杀菌可有效灭活H5N1病毒,预计不会出现牛奶短缺。由于受感染奶牛主要通过生乳排出病毒,卫生部门建议消费者和宠物主人避免使用未经巴氏杀菌的乳制品。 美国疾病控制与预防中心和华盛顿州卫生部认为,普通公众面临的风险较低;美国尚未发现人际传播。奶牛场工作人员的暴露风险较高,建议佩戴手套、口罩、护目装备,并穿着防液体渗透的连体防护服。2026年,华盛顿州已在亚基马县奶牛养殖场工作人员中记录到三例人感染病例,其中一名有基础疾病的患者死亡。 过去30天内,美国农业部已确认七个州的26个奶牛群发生感染,其中邻近的俄勒冈州出现一例。自2024年3月以来,全美累计已有26个州的1,236个奶牛群受到影响。 关注我们的Telegram 关注我们的Instagram 关注我们的LinkedIn 打印 本周要闻 14.10.2026 Radhika Krishnaswamy指出AI可以发现隐性损失,但需要人为决策 19.09.2026 Health officials say the person had mild symptoms and received a preventative treatment. Image A pair of dairy cows. | WIKIMEDIA COMMONS by Amelia Templeton|Oregon Public Broadcasting November 21, 2026 State health officials have confirmed Oregon’s first human case of avian influenza this year in a Morrow County dairy worker. It is the first known case in Oregon involving transmission from a cow to a human. The person has a mild case involving conjunctivitis and upper respiratory symptoms, officials said, and did not need to go to the hospital. Avian influenza has been circulating and causing deadly outbreaks among wild waterfowl and domesticated poultry — and sporadic human cases — for decades. In 2024, Oregon confirmed a single human case of avian flu linked to a poultry outbreak. A recent strain of the virus has caused multiple outbreaks among dairy cows in the U.S. and is infecting other mammals. The virus is not deadly in cows, but it affects their mammary glands and udders, causing mastitis. Avian flu has periodically spilled over into people who have close contact with infected birds and cows, often farm workers. It does not currently have the ability to transmit between humans, and Oregon health officials say the current risk to the public is low. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention have reported 74 confirmed cases of avian flu in humans in the U.S., primarily in people in direct contact with poultry or cows. There have been three reported fatalities, including a farmworker in Washington’s Yakima Valley. Oregon officials say they were able to quickly detect the Morrow County case and give the person a preventative flu treatment, oseltamivir. The treatment works best when it is administered early in the course of a person’s illness. Health workers also offered the treatment to other members of the infected worker’s household out of an abundance of caution. Health officials said the case illustrates the value of the state’s ongoing surveillance effort for avian flu. The Oregon Department of Agriculture tests milk from dairies statewide for avian influenza every week. One of those routine tests flagged the outbreak among dairy cows at the Morrow County farm, the state’s first, earlier this month. The state agency then placed the farm under quarantine and worked with public health workers to provide personal protective equipment and to spread the word about what symptoms farm workers should be monitoring for and how to report them. Dr. Dean Sidelinger, Oregon’s state epidemiologist, said health workers will likely be working with the farm for at least six more weeks to continue to offer testing and treatment with the goal of catching any more human cases early. Dr. Ryan Scholz, the state veterinarian for the Oregon Department of Agriculture, says workers have been encouraged to report even minor symptoms. “We don’t want it to be missed and be too far down the road to be able to do anything about it,” he said. No other dairy herds in Oregon have tested positive for the virus yet in the two weeks since the state first detected the outbreak in Morrow County. Scholz said genetic sequencing shows that the outbreak in Oregon is connected to the outbreak in Washington’s Yakima Valley, where dozens of herds have recently tested positive for the virus. Scholz said there’s no indication of any cattle moving from Yakima to the dairy in Morrow County, leading him to believe it may have traveled across state lines on a person’s muddy boots, a vehicle, or unclean farm equipment. “Typically that’s how we see this virus move within dairy sheds,” he said. According to Scholz, the Morrow County dairy is relatively isolated, which he hopes will reduce the risk of further transmission to other farms in Oregon. The risk to workers on other farms is relatively low, Scholz said. Still, health officials are encouraging anyone who works with cattle or birds to get their seasonal flu vaccine. That shot does not protect against avian flu, but it can help reduce the risk of a person getting sick with human influenza viruses and the avian flu virus simultaneously. Co-infection is a major concern of public health officials and virologists because different flu viruses can swap segments of their genome, and that could in theory provide avian influenza a pathway to becoming transmissible between people. supplementary_news.excerpt: 新华社日内瓦11月24日电 世界卫生组织24日说,美国向该组织通报了3例人感染甲型H5禽流感病毒病例,其中1人死亡。目前世卫组织评估该病毒对一般公众的风险较低。 根据世卫组织官网的消息,这3人均为成年人,在美国华盛顿州亚基马县一家奶牛场工作,该地区近期已在奶牛中检测到高致病性H5N1型禽流感病毒。迄今尚无证据表明存在人际传播。世卫组织将继续密切监测。

supplementary_news.content: H5禽流感病毒血凝素-神经氨酸酶(HA-NA)配对兼容性的分子决定因素:HA糖基化位点与NA stalk长度的协同调控 《EMBO JOURNAL》:Molecular determinants of surface glycoprotein compatibility may explain the emergence of highly pathogenic avian influenza A viruses 【字体: 大 中 小 】 时间:2026年11月26日 来源:EMBO JOURNAL 8.4 为了促进科学的传播,生物通采集了这篇文章 订阅BioHot点这里解锁原文链接推送! “畅读会员”点此登录查看原文链接 Article Open access 禽流感病毒(IAVs)跨宿主物种的传播与扩散,以高致病性分支2.3.4.4b H5N1病毒的流行为典型代表,其部分取决于表面糖蛋白血凝素(HA)与神经氨酸酶(NA)之间的功能兼容性。然而,支配HA-NA优先配对的分子决定因素仍不清楚。研究人员发现,具有6个糖基化位点的2.3.4.4b分支H5 HA在鸟类与哺乳动物中优先与全长(long-stalk)N1 NA配对。相比之下,来源于较早分支的具有7个糖基化位点的H5 HA优先与具有stalk缺失(short-stalk)的N1 NA配对。研究结果表明,在禽流感病毒中观察到的HA S/T160A突变消除了N158糖基化位点,并有利于与long-stalk N1配对,从而改善分子兼容性并增强病毒适应度。N158糖基化位点是Gs/GD系H5病毒与short-stalk N1蛋白优先配对的基础。这些发现表明,禽流感病毒中的HA-NA配对并非完全随机过程,而是受HA糖基化状态与NA stalk长度的制约,这对病毒适应度及分支2.3.4.4b H5N1病毒的涌现具有启示意义。 禽流感病毒(Influenza A viruses, IAVs)作为重要的人畜共患病原,其跨物种传播与持续进化始终是公共卫生领域关注的核心问题。高致病性禽流感(Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, HPAI)H5N1病毒,特别是当前全球广泛传播的分支2.3.4.4b,已造成大量禽类及多种哺乳动物感染死亡,并具备潜在的人畜共患传播风险。流感病毒表面糖蛋白血凝素(Hemagglutinin, HA)负责识别宿主细胞受体,神经氨酸酶(Neuraminidase, NA)则促进子代病毒释放,二者之间的功能平衡是病毒适应度的关键决定因素。尽管HA-NA兼容性被广泛认为是流感病毒适应度的重要决定因素,但决定二者优先配对的分子特征尚不清楚。研究人员注意到,当前流行的2.3.4.4b H5病毒优先与全长stalk的N1配对,而此前的H5N1病毒主要与stalk缺失型N1配对,这种转变背后的分子基础亟待阐明。 【泛素酶和PROTAC?:靶向治疗的新前沿】,免费下载SignalChem Biotech(义翘神州全资子公司)的最新进展总结 >>> 领 取 为系统解析这一问题,研究人员基于GISAID数据库开展了大尺度禽流感病毒序列分析,涵盖约17,843条H5-NA配对序列,重点关注H5 HA糖基化位点数量、位置与N1 NA stalk长度之间的关联。同时,利用反向遗传系统(reverse genetics)构建重组病毒,以A/PuertoRico/8/34(H1N1)的6个内部基因片段为骨架,替换不同来源H5N1病毒的HA与NA片段,在MDCK细胞、Calu-3细胞、鸡胚及BALB/c小鼠中评估病毒复制动力学与致病性。此外,研究人员采用分子动力学模拟(Molecular Dynamics Simulation, MDS)结合MM-PBSA结合自由能计算,分析HA与N1的结构动态及配体结合特性,并通过MUNANA荧光底物法检测NA酶活性与神经氨酸酶抑制剂敏感性。 研究首先揭示了H5病毒与不同长度N1蛋白的配对规律。在2020年之前的Gs/GD系H5N1病毒中,绝大多数与33个氨基酸残基的short-stalk N1配对;而当前流行的2.3.4.4b H5N1病毒则严格与53个氨基酸残基的long-stalk N1配对,且该配对模式在狐狸、貂、海狮、牛等多种哺乳动物感染株中均保持一致。系统发育分析进一步证实,这种配对转变与H5 HA糖基化位点数量的变化密切相关。具有6个糖基化位点(6-GLS)的2.3.4.4b H5 HA优先与long-stalk N1配对,而具有7个糖基化位点(7-GLS)的H5 HA则偏好short-stalk N1。值得注意的是,HA S/T160A突变(在禽流感病毒中广泛存在)可消除N158糖基化位点,使原本偏好short-stalk N1的H5 HA转向与long-stalk N1配对,提示N158糖基化位点是调控HA-NA配对的关键分子开关。分子动力学模拟显示,N158糖基化位点的缺失增强了HA与唾液酸的结合亲和力,同时使受体结合口袋构象更为刚性,这可能与stalk长度变化引起的NA功能改变形成互补平衡。 在病毒适应度验证方面,重组病毒感染实验表明,2.3.4.4b分支的long-stalk N1与缺失N158糖基化位点的H5 HA组合在体外哺乳动物细胞及鸡胚中表现出更高的复制效价,在小鼠肺部与鼻甲组织中的病毒载量也显著高于short-stalk N1组合。NA酶活性测定发现,short-stalk N1表现出较高的MUNANA水解活性,而long-stalk N1活性较低,提示当前流行的H5N1病毒可能通过降低NA酶活性来匹配HA结合亲和力的变化,从而维持HA-NA功能平衡。结构分析进一步揭示,2.3.4.4b分支的long-stalk N1在stalk区域存在A46P等关键突变,使其构象偏好性与早期long-stalk N1不同,这可能是其能够与6-GLS H5 HA成功配对的结构基础。 讨论部分指出,H5 HA糖基化模式的演变与NA stalk长度的变化共同决定了禽流感病毒的宿主适应与进化方向。第7个糖基化位点从HA 93位(VE结构域)向158位(RBD)的转移,以及随后6-GLS变体的出现,均发生在获得long-stalk N1之前,表明HA分子变化先于NA stalk改变以维持功能平衡。N158糖基化位点的丢失不仅增强了HA与α2-6连接唾液酸的结合能力,还可能影响HA头部丝状组装,从而调节病毒与宿主细胞表面寡聚受体的多价相互作用。这些发现共同表明,禽流感病毒HA-NA配对并非随机事件,而是受HA糖基化状态与NA stalk长度的协同制约。监测HA糖基化位点模式及NA stalk长度等分子特征,可为预测新型禽流感病毒的出现与传播潜力提供重要线索,对流感大流行的预警防控具有重要参考价值。 禽流感病毒(Influenza A viruses, IAVs)作为重要的人畜共患病原,其跨物种传播与持续进化始终是公共卫生领域关注的核心问题。高致病性禽流感(Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza, 加拿大警告感恩节出行者:因禽流感暴发,不要将火鸡从美国带入境 2026-11-27 06:20 来源: shazhouyue 链接复制成功 发布于:河南省 加拿大警告感恩节出行者,鉴于新一轮禽流感疫情暴发,不要将火鸡剩菜从美国带过边境。 渥太华——感恩节期间跨越美加边境的人必须注意加拿大对食品入境的限制。受影响的产品包括火鸡菜肴的剩菜和自制禽类食品。 这些规定旨在防止禽流感传播,同样适用于在美国与亲友聚会后返回加拿大的加拿大居民。自制火鸡三明治和其他含禽肉的餐食不得入境。 鉴于加拿大和美国暴发新一轮高致病性禽流感疫情,相关限制措施继续生效。 加拿大边境服务局(CBSA)在10月发布的一份旅行提示中表示:“含有禽肉的自制食品或剩菜不得带入加拿大。”未申报食品的旅客每次违规可能面临最高1300加元(约 6105.95人民币)的罚款。 美国和加拿大暴发新一轮禽流感疫情 受影响地区包括加利福尼亚州普莱瑟县、华盛顿州皮尔斯县、爱达荷州古丁县和俄勒冈州克拉克马斯县。此前有报道称上述地区暴发了H5N1亚型高致病性禽流感疫情。 该机构发言人表示,已联系相关部门,并将继续关注事态发展。他补充说:“将根据疫情发展采取适当措施。” 加拿大食品检验局(CFIA)于11月18日在阿尔伯塔省设立了一个新的禽流感控制区。墨西哥同日对来自魁北克的活禽和禽肉实施了进口限制。 哪些感恩节食品在加拿大边境被禁止入境 加拿大食品检验局建议旅客不要将违禁禽类产品带入加拿大,并建议在从美国出发前了解进口限制。CBSA表示:“入境加拿大时请申报您携带的所有物品。”驾车者对其车辆中的所有物品负责。 加拿大食品检验局明确将餐厅食物和剩菜以及含禽肉的自制食品列为禁止入境物品。来自路边摊、农场和私人养殖的禽类产品同样受到限制。但这些规定并不意味着全面禁止美国禽类产品。 旅客仍可携带某些在食品零售店购买且以商业常规包装出售的产品进入加拿大,包括冷冻整火鸡、烤鸡、切片熟食肉、鸡蛋和包装鸡胸肉,前提是符合加拿大对包装、标签和个人进口量的要求。 据加拿大食品检验局规定,允许供人食用的产品必须采用零售包装,并标注“美国产品”标识。这些产品可从美国任何州进口,无论该州是否暴发禽流感。 个人进口量上限为每人20公斤肉类和禽类产品以及五打鸡蛋。相关限制同样适用于宠物食品。含禽肉的熟制干粮和罐头食品在遵守进口规定的前提下允许入境,前提是动物随旅客同行。该机构表示:“旅客在任何时候都不得携带生宠物食品入境。” 感恩节旅客在边境面临罚款 CBSA警告称,边境官员可能没收未申报的食品以及动植物产品。旅客还可能“需要缴纳最高1300加元(约 6105.95人民币)的罚款”。罚款金额从轻微违规的500加元(约 2348.44人民币)、严重违规的800加元(约 3757.51人民币)到非常严重违规的1300加元(约 6105.95人民币)不等。多次违规可能导致额外罚款。 加拿大边境当局还呼吁驾车者在出发前了解等候时间。为避免拥堵,通常建议清晨过境。加拿大边境当局在10月的感恩节提示中表示,驾车者应在出发前查看等候时间。返回搜狐,查看更多 首赞 +1 点赞失败 阅读 (14) 平台声明 该文观点仅代表作者本人,搜狐号系信息发布平台,搜狐仅提供信息存储空间服务。 内容举报 by Taboolaby Taboola Sponsored LinksSponsored Meyer The Green First State Mixtape Hometown Heroes Money & Politics in Delaware How Not to Kill Your Community (DCF) About Us The DPM Team Board of Directors Community Advisory Board Annual Reports Employment Contact Us The DPM Team Board of Directors Community Advisory Board Annual Reports Employment Contact Us Stay Connected Newsletters DPM Mobile App Facebook → Instagram → YouTube → LinkedIn → Newsletters DPM Mobile App Facebook → Instagram → YouTube → LinkedIn → Ways to Support Become a Member Matching Gifts IRA Donations (QCD) Stocks & Donor-Advised Funds (DAF) Legacy Giving & Estate Planning Adopt a Program → Donate a Vehicle → Underwriting / Corporate Sponsorship Become a Member Matching Gifts IRA Donations (QCD) Stocks & Donor-Advised Funds (DAF) Legacy Giving & Estate Planning Adopt a Program → Donate a Vehicle → Underwriting / Corporate Sponsorship News Poultry owners are advised to be vigilant for avian flu season Delaware Public Media | By Joe Irizarry Published November 26, 2026 at 7:31 PM EST Facebook Twitter LinkedIn Email Listen • 1:07 Delmarva Avian Influenza Joint Information Center The Delaware Department of Agriculture provides poultry safety tips with avian flu season already arriving in the state. The season usually arrives with colder temperatures, and tips for preventing avian flu are important since it’s a highly contagious airborne respiratory virus. It spreads quickly among birds through nasal and eye secretions and manure. It can also be spread from flock to flock, affecting poultry like chickens, ducks and turkeys, as well as some wild bird species. During avian flu season, Delaware’s Department of Agriculture advises all poultry owners to increase their vigilance. The Ag Department’s chief of community relations Michael Lewis also has some tips. "Number one is to exclude your flock from spaces where wild or migratory birds, especially waterfowl, have access. Just keep them within fenced in areas that you already have. Make sure you're disinfecting equipment, vehicles and footwear and other items prior to contact with flocks. Limit your travel between farms and make sure you're taking - if you have to travel - make sure you're taking preventative measures like covering your feet and everything. Make sure you're washing up," said Lewis. Other tips include isolating any animals with signs of illness, contacting your veterinarian and record any activity on or off your farm. Lewis also has tips for the general public. "The number one tip for the general public is if you see a sick or dead wild bird or a bird of any kind, don't touch it, or don't try to help it, as difficult as that may be. Just please contact the appropriate state agency," said Lewis. If backyard flock owners notice dead birds or unusual signs in their health, they should email or call the Delaware Poultry Health Hotline. Commercial poultry producers should follow the procedures of contacting the company they grow for when they notice the signs of the virus.
